q: Pune (Maharashtra) is called:
opts: 'Oxford of the East' for its numerous educational institutions
explain: Pune is called 'Oxford of the East' for its many universities and colleges (Pune University, Symbiosis, Fergusson College, etc.). It is also a major IT and automobile hub. Peshwas made it their capital.

q: Salem district (Tamil Nadu) is famous for:
explain: Salem district is known for the Salem Steel Plant (SAIL plant, 1981), Salem mangoes, silk weaving (Kancheepuram-type in Salem), and marble/granite quarrying. Salem is the 5th largest city in Tamil Nadu.

q: India's highest road (motorable) is:
opts: Umling La Pass, Ladakh (19,024 ft / 5,799 m)
explain: Umling La Pass in Ladakh (5,799 m / 19,024 ft) is the world's highest motorable road, surpassing Khardung La. It was made motorable by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in 2021.

q: The Ten Degree Channel separates:
explain: The Ten Degree Channel (at 10°N latitude) separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands. The Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.

q: The Sundarbans is located in:
explain: The Sundarbans (world's largest mangrove forest) straddles the India-Bangladesh border in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

q: The world's longest railway platform is in:
explain: Gorakhpur railway station in Uttar Pradesh has the world's longest railway platform at 1,366.33 m. Kharagpur (1,072 m) was previously the record holder. Hubli also has a very long platform.

q: The largest continent in the world is:
explain: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 44.6 million km² (about 30% of Earth's total land area). It is also the most populous continent.

q: The Greater Himalayas (Himadri) include:
opts: Everest, K2, Kangchenjunga, Nanda Devi — average 6,000+ m
explain: Greater Himalayas (Himadri) is the innermost and highest zone — all peaks above 6,000 m, including Everest, K2, Kangchenjunga, Nanda Devi, Dhaulagiri, Makalu, Cho Oyu. Perpetually snow-covered.

q: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet in which region?
explain: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu/Karnataka border region.

q: India's largest port (by cargo handled) is:
explain: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT/Nhava Sheva) near Mumbai was India's largest container port for many years. However, Mundra Port (Adani Ports, Gujarat) has recently surpassed JNPT in total cargo.

q: The Siachen glacier is in:
explain: Siachen glacier (world's highest battlefield) is in the Karakoram Range. India controls most of it since Operation Meghdoot (1984). It is the world's second-longest non-polar glacier.

q: The highest point in Tamil Nadu is:
explain: Doddabetta (2,637 m) in the Nilgiris district is the highest peak in Tamil Nadu and the second-highest in South India. Anamudi (2,695 m) is higher but is in Kerala.

q: Shipki La Pass connects:
explain: Shipki La Pass (5,669 m) in Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh, connects India with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. The Sutlej river enters India through this pass.

q: Which state has the largest reserves of iron ore in India?
explain: Odisha has the largest reserves of iron ore in India (about 33% of total). Major mines: Barbil-Sundergarh region. Karnataka (Bellary-Hospet) and Chhattisgarh-Jharkhand are also major producers.

q: Which direction does the sun rise?
explain: The sun rises in the East due to Earth's west-to-east rotation.

q: Sandy/desert soil is found mainly in:
explain: Sandy (arid/desert) soil is mainly found in the Thar Desert (Rajasthan) and some coastal areas. It has poor water retention, low fertility, and high sand content. It requires irrigation and soil conservation.

q: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through how many Indian states?
explain: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. It also passes through West Bengal and Tripura.

q: Lipulekh Pass is used for:
explain: Lipulekh Pass (5,334 m) in Uttarakhand (Pithoragarh district) connects India with Tibet (China). It is used for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. It is also disputed between India and Nepal.

id: geography-499-The Gulf of Mannar is be
q: The Gulf of Mannar is between:
explain: The Gulf of Mannar lies between southeastern India (Tamil Nadu coast) and the western coast of Sri Lanka. It is known for rich marine biodiversity and pearl fishing.

q: India is the world's largest producer of coffee in Asia. Major coffee-growing state is:
explain: Karnataka produces about 70% of India's coffee (primarily in Coorg/Kodagu, Chikmagalur, Hassan). Kerala (20%) and Tamil Nadu (5-6%) are other major producers. India grows both Arabica and Robusta.

q: The Tehri Dam (India's highest dam) is built on which river?
explain: Tehri Dam (260.5 m high) is built on the Bhagirathi river in Uttarakhand — India's tallest and one of the world's tallest dams. The reservoir is called Tehri Lake.

q:
With reference to Indian islands, consider the following statements:
1. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are of volcanic/tectonic origin.
2. The Lakshadweep Islands are coral-origin islands located in the Arabian Sea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — Andaman & Nicobar Islands are tectonic/volcanic in origin (an extension of the Arakan Yoma range), while Lakshadweep islands are coral (atoll) formations in the Arabian Sea.

q: The Chilika Lake is connected to the sea by a channel near:
opts: Satpara mouth near Puri (Odisha coast, Bay of Bengal)
explain: Chilika Lake in Odisha is connected to the Bay of Bengal via a 32 km long channel near Satpara/Sipakuda. The connection point keeps changing due to sediment. The lake spans Puri, Khurda, and Ganjam districts.

q:
Match List-I (National Highway/Corridor) with List-II (connecting route) and select the correct answer:

List-I
A. Golden Quadrilateral
B. North-South Corridor
C. East-West Corridor
D. NH 44 (formerly NH 7)

List-II
1. Srinagar to Kanniyakumari
2. Porbandar/Silchar to Silchar/Porbandar (east-west link)
3. Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata mega-highway
4. Srinagar to Kanniyakumari (longest NH)
explain: Golden Quadrilateral connects the four metro cities (Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata); North-South Corridor links Srinagar to Kanniyakumari; East-West Corridor links Porbandar and Silchar; NH 44 is the longest national highway, itself running Srinagar to Kanniyakumari. Correct: A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

q: The highest waterfall in the world is:
explain: Angel Falls (Salto Ángel) in Venezuela is the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 m. Named after American aviator Jimmie Angel who spotted it in 1933. Niagara is famous for volume, not height.

q: The Thar Desert is primarily located in:
explain: The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) is primarily in western Rajasthan (India), extending into parts of Pakistan. In India, it also covers small areas of Gujarat, Haryana, and Punjab.

q: Bhilai Steel Plant was established with assistance from:
explain: Bhilai Steel Plant (Chhattisgarh) was set up with Soviet Union's assistance in 1955. Durgapur (UK assistance) and Rourkela (West Germany) were established around the same time.

q: The 'Shiwalik' hills (also called Sub-Himalayan range) are the:
explain: The Himalayas have three parallel ranges: Greater Himalayas (Himadri - highest), Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks/Sub-Himalayas - southernmost, youngest, 600-1500m). Shiwaliks formed by erosion debris from older Himalayan ranges.

q:
Statement-I: Coal is classified into different grades such as anthracite, bituminous, lignite and peat.
Statement-II: The classification is based primarily on carbon content, which also determines calorific value.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Both statements are correct, and carbon content (Statement-II) is exactly the basis on which the coal grades in Statement-I are differentiated, with anthracite having the highest carbon/calorific value and peat the lowest.

q: 'Doon' valleys are characteristic of:
opts: Longitudinal valleys between Shivalik and Lesser Himalayas
explain: 'Doon' (or 'Dun') valleys are longitudinal synclinal valleys lying between the Shivalik (Outer Himalayas) and the Lesser Himalayas. Dehra Dun (Uttarakhand) is the most famous Doon valley.

q: The most densely populated state in India is:
explain: Bihar has the highest population density in India (1,106 persons/sq km as per 2011 census), followed by West Bengal (1,028). UP has the highest absolute population.

q: Saline/alkaline soil (Usar/Reh) is formed in:
opts: Waterlogged and arid areas with high salt content
explain: Saline/alkaline soils (Usar, Reh, Kallar) form in waterlogged and arid areas where salts accumulate due to high evaporation or poor drainage. Common in parts of UP, Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, and Rajasthan.

id: geography-22-The Chambal River is a t
q: The Chambal River is a tributary of:
explain: The Chambal River (originating from Vindhya Range in Madhya Pradesh) is a major tributary of the Yamuna River. The Chambal valley is known for its ravines (badlands).

id: geography-37-Which type of delta is t
q: Which type of delta is the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta classified as?
opts: Arcuate (fan-shaped) delta — the largest in the world
explain: The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta is an arcuate (fan-shaped) delta and the world's largest river delta (~105,000 km²). It hosts the Sundarbans mangrove. Arcuate deltas form when wave action spreads sediment evenly on both sides.

q: Tamil Nadu's Coromandel Coast receives maximum rainfall in:
explain: The Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu's eastern coast) receives maximum rainfall from the northeast monsoon in October-December. This is the retreating monsoon season for the rest of India but the main rainy season for Tamil Nadu.

q: How many states does India have (as of 2024)?
explain: India has 28 states and 8 Union Territories (as of 2024 after the reorganisation of J&K into two UTs in 2019).

q: The 'K-T Boundary' in geological stratigraphy refers to:
opts: The boundary between Jurassic and Cretaceous periods
The boundary between Cretaceous and Paleogene periods — linked to mass extinction
The time India separated from Gondwana
The age of the Himalayan orogeny
explain: The K-Pg (Cretaceous-Paleogene) boundary, formerly called K-T boundary, marks the mass extinction event 66 million years ago that wiped out non-avian dinosaurs. The Deccan Traps eruptions and the Chicxulub asteroid impact are associated with this event.

q: The Westerlies (Prevailing Westerlies) blow from:
explain: The Westerlies blow from the sub-tropical high pressure belt (~30°) towards the sub-polar low pressure belt (~60°) in both hemispheres. They blow from the southwest in N hemisphere and northwest in S hemisphere.

q: Yellow Revolution in India is associated with:
explain: Yellow Revolution refers to the rapid increase in oilseed production in India (primarily sunflower, mustard, groundnut, soybean). The Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986) launched by PM Rajiv Gandhi triggered this.

q: The newly created capital of Andhra Pradesh is:
explain: Amaravati (on the Krishna river, between Vijayawada and Guntur) is the proposed new capital of Andhra Pradesh, after Hyderabad became the capital of Telangana. Its construction has been contested politically.

q: The 'Oil and Natural Gas Corporation' (ONGC) produces most of India's petroleum from:
opts: Mumbai High (offshore, Arabian Sea) — about 60% of production
explain: Mumbai High (Bombay High) offshore oilfields in the Arabian Sea produce about 60% of India's total crude oil. Other producing areas: Gujarat (Ankleshwar, Kalol), Assam (Digboi — oldest oilfield in Asia, 1889), Rajasthan (Barmer/Mangala).

q: Which ocean surrounds India on three sides?
explain: India is a peninsula surrounded by water on three sides: Bay of Bengal (east), Arabian Sea (west), and Indian Ocean (south). This has made India a maritime trading nation since ancient times.

q: Black cotton soil (Regur) is most suitable for growing:
explain: Black cotton soil (Regur) — found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat, Karnataka) — is highly fertile for cotton. It retains moisture well, has high clay content, and swells when wet.

q: The Western Ghats is one of the world's 'Biodiversity Hotspots' because:
opts: It has the largest forest area
It has exceptional species richness and endemism
It is the highest mountain range in India
It is the oldest geological formation
explain: The Western Ghats (UNESCO World Heritage Site, 2012) is one of the 36 global biodiversity hotspots. It has ~5,000 flowering plant species (1,700 endemic), 77% endemic amphibians, 32% endemic fish. Also home to tigers, elephants, lion-tailed macaque.

q: The Lakshadweep Islands are formed by:
explain: Lakshadweep Islands are coral islands (atolls) formed by coral reefs built on submerged volcanic peaks. They are India's smallest Union Territory. Agatti Island has the only airport.

q:
Statement-I: The Western Ghats host exceptionally high levels of endemic species.
Statement-II: Its long isolation, varied altitude and high rainfall gradient have allowed unique speciation over geological time.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Both statements are correct, and the ecological/geological factors in Statement-II (isolation, altitude variation, rainfall gradient) are the standard scientific explanation for the high endemism described in Statement-I.

q: The island country of Sri Lanka was formerly known as:
explain: Sri Lanka was called Ceylon (in English, from Portuguese 'Ceilão') until 1972 when it became a republic and adopted the name Sri Lanka. The ancient name was Serendip (Arabian/Persian) and Taprobane (Greek).

q: The longest river in Europe is:
explain: Volga river (3,692 km) in Russia is Europe's longest river. It flows into the Caspian Sea (not the ocean). The Danube (2,860 km) is Europe's second-longest river and flows through 10 countries.

q: The Musi river flows through:
explain: Musi river flows through the heart of Hyderabad. It is a tributary of the Krishna river. The historic Golconda Fort, Charminar, and most of the old city of Hyderabad are on the banks of the Musi.

id: geography-165-The major soil type in T
q: The major soil type in Tamil Nadu is:
explain: Red loamy soil dominates Tamil Nadu (~60% of State). Red soils are deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter but respond well to irrigation. Black cotton soil is found in northern Tamil Nadu.

q:
Consider the following statements on population distribution factors:
1. Fertile alluvial plains generally support higher population densities than arid or mountainous regions.
2. Availability of water is a key factor influencing settlement patterns historically.
3. Climate extremes (very cold or very hot/dry) tend to discourage dense human settlement.
4. Population density in India is uniformly high across all states without significant regional variation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — standard population geography principles. Statement 4 is incorrect — India shows huge variation in density, from Bihar (~1,106/sq km) to Arunachal Pradesh (very low). Hence only three.

q: The Vindhya Range separates:
explain: The Vindhya mountain range (in Madhya Pradesh) separates North India (Indo-Gangetic Plain) from South India (Deccan Plateau). Historically it was a major cultural boundary.

q:
With reference to world rivers, consider the following statements:
1. The Nile is generally considered the longest river in the world.
2. The Amazon carries the largest volume of water discharge of any river in the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — the Nile is traditionally cited as the longest river by length, while the Amazon carries by far the greatest discharge volume of any river.

q: The 'El Niño' phenomenon is associated with abnormal warming of surface water in:
explain: El Niño is associated with abnormal warming of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean off the coast of South America, disrupting global weather patterns including Indian monsoon.

q: The deepest port in India is:
explain: Visakhapatnam Port (Vizag) is India's deepest natural port. It has a natural draft of about 17.5 m and is a major port on the east coast. It handles iron ore, coal, and petroleum products.

q: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous ranges that run along which coast?
explain: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous ranges running along the eastern coast (Coromandel Coast) of India, from Odisha to Tamil Nadu.

q: The Kaveri-Bhavani-Amaravathi river basin supports irrigation in:
opts: Coimbatore, Erode, Tiruppur, and the Kaveri delta districts
explain: The Kaveri and its tributaries Bhavani and Amaravathi irrigate Coimbatore, Erode, Tiruppur, Salem, Karur, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, and Nagapattinam districts — the main agricultural areas of Tamil Nadu.

q: 'Subduction zone' is where:
opts: A denser plate slides under a lighter plate
explain: A subduction zone is where an oceanic plate (denser) slides under a continental or another oceanic plate. This causes deep-focus earthquakes, trenches (like Mariana Trench), and volcanic arcs (Ring of Fire).

q: Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory of India. Its capital is:
explain: Kavaratti is the capital of Lakshadweep, India's smallest Union Territory by area (32 sq km). Agatti island has the only airport. The islands are coral atolls in the Arabian Sea.

q: The Brahmaputra river valley in Assam forms:
opts: A narrow alluvial plain (Himalayas to Shillong Plateau)
explain: The Brahmaputra valley in Assam is a narrow alluvial plain (~80 km wide, 700 km long) between the Himalayas to the north and the Shillong Plateau/Meghalaya hills to the south.

id: geography-551-The Gulf of Kutch is fam
q: The Gulf of Kutch is famous for:
opts: Tidal energy potential, Kandla Port, and flamingos
explain: Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat) has one of the highest tidal ranges in India (7-8 m), making it ideal for tidal energy. Kandla Port (Deendayal Port) is India's second-largest port by cargo. The gulf also has flamingos and corals.

q: India shares the longest border with which country?
explain: India shares its longest land border with Bangladesh (4,156 km), followed by China (3,488 km), Pakistan (3,323 km), Nepal (1,751 km), Myanmar (1,643 km), Bhutan (699 km), and Afghanistan (106 km, disputed).

q: The highest peak in South India (outside Himalayas) is:
explain: Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anamalai Hills, Idukki district, Kerala is the highest peak in South India and the highest peak south of the Himalayas in India.

q:
With reference to the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passing through India, consider the following statements:
1. It passes through eight Indian states, including Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal.
2. It divides India roughly into tropical and subtropical climatic zones.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — the Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states/UTs (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram), and it broadly demarcates the tropical south from the subtropical north.

q: Tobacco production in India is mainly in:
explain: Andhra Pradesh (especially Guntur) and Telangana produce about 50%+ of India's tobacco (Virginia/flue-cured variety). India is the world's third-largest tobacco producer after China and Brazil.

q: 'Great Circle' routes are used by aircraft because:
opts: They are the shortest paths between two points on a sphere
explain: Great Circle routes are the shortest paths between two points on a sphere (Earth). Aircraft flying long-distance routes follow great circle paths to save fuel and time, even though the routes may appear curved on flat maps.

q: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was India's first biosphere reserve, established in:
explain: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (covering parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka) was India's first biosphere reserve, established in 1986. It covers 5,520 sq km and is a UNESCO Man and Biosphere Reserve.

id: geography-187-Mettur Dam is built on w
q: Mettur Dam is built on which river?
explain: Mettur Dam (Stanley Reservoir) is built on the Kaveri river in Salem district, Tamil Nadu. Opened in 1934, it is one of India's largest dams and supplies water for irrigation in the Kaveri delta.

q: Courtallam (Kutralam) waterfalls in Tamil Nadu are near:
explain: Courtallam (Kutralam) is near Tenkasi in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu. Famous for medicinal waterfalls, it is called the 'Spa of South India'. The falls are formed by the Chittar river.

q: The river Beas originates from:
opts: Beas Kund, near Rohtang Pass, Himachal Pradesh
explain: The Beas (Vipasa) originates from the Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass in Kullu, Himachal Pradesh. It flows through Kullu Valley and joins the Sutlej near Harike (Punjab). Part of the Indus system.

id: geography-67-The soil found in the Ga
q: The soil found in the Gangetic plains is:
explain: Alluvial soil (brought by rivers) is found in the Gangetic plains. It is the most fertile soil type in India, ideal for wheat, rice, and sugarcane cultivation.

q: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is for protection of:
opts: Wetlands (marshes, lakes, rivers, peat bogs, coastal areas)
explain: The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (signed 1971, Ramsar, Iran) is an international treaty for conservation of wetlands. India has 75 Ramsar sites. Chilika Lake (Odisha) was India's first Ramsar site (1981).

q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands experience heavy rainfall because:
opts: They receive both southwest and northeast monsoon rains
They are near the equator only
explain: Andaman and Nicobar Islands receive rainfall from both the southwest monsoon (May-October) and the northeast monsoon (November-December), giving them about 300 cm of annual rainfall. They are near the equator.

q: The Himalayan region receives most of its snowfall from:
explain: The Himalayas receive heavy snowfall in winter from Western Disturbances — cyclonic systems from the Mediterranean Sea. In summer, the Southwest Monsoon brings rain to the lower Himalayas. The higher reaches are always cold.

q: Dispur (part of Guwahati) is the capital of:
explain: Dispur (a locality within Guwahati) is the capital of Assam. Guwahati itself is the largest city in Assam and Northeast India. Assam's state legislative assembly is in Dispur.

q: The country with the largest area in the world is:
explain: Russia (17.1 million sq km) is the world's largest country by area, followed by Canada (10 million sq km) and USA (9.8 million sq km). Russia spans 11 time zones.

q: Tiruvannamalai district in Tamil Nadu is famous for:
explain: Tiruvannamalai is famous for the Annamalai Hill (Arunachala) and the Annamalayar Temple — a major Shaivite pilgrimage site. The hill is sacred as a manifestation of Agni (fire). Ramana Maharshi ashram is also here.

q:
With reference to renewable energy resources in India, consider the following statements:
1. Rajasthan and Gujarat have among the highest installed solar power capacities in India.
2. Tamil Nadu has traditionally been a leader in installed wind power capacity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — Rajasthan and Gujarat lead in solar capacity due to high solar insolation, and Tamil Nadu has long been among the top states for wind power capacity.

q: The One-horned Rhinoceros in India is mainly in:
explain: The Indian One-horned Rhinoceros population is mainly in Kaziranga National Park, Assam (~2,400 rhinos — 70% of the world's population), Manas (Assam), and Jaldapara (West Bengal).

q: India's first National Park was:
explain: Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand) was established in 1936 as 'Hailey National Park' — India's first national park. Named after Jim Corbett (British hunter-naturalist). It is a Project Tiger reserve.

q: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) is where:
opts: Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean meet
Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean meet
explain: Kanyakumari (southernmost tip of Indian mainland) is the confluece point of the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean. It is famous for the sunrise/sunset view and the Vivekananda Rock Memorial.

q:
With reference to jet streams, consider the following statements:
1. The sub-tropical westerly jet stream influences winter weather over North India, including western disturbances.
2. The tropical easterly jet stream flows over peninsular India during the south-west monsoon season.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — the sub-tropical westerly jet steers winter western disturbances into North India, and the tropical easterly jet (Somali/African jet-linked) is associated with the active monsoon season.

q: India's population according to the 2011 census was approximately:
explain: India's population as per Census 2011 was 1,210,854,977 (about 1.21 billion). India's population density was 382 persons/km². The most populous state was Uttar Pradesh (19.98 crore).

q: Trade winds blow from:
explain: Trade winds blow from the sub-tropical high pressure belts (around 30°N and 30°S) towards the equatorial low pressure belt. In the N hemisphere, they blow from NE; in the S hemisphere, from SE.

q: The rain shadow area (leeward side) of the Western Ghats includes:
explain: The Western Ghats block the southwest monsoon. The windward (western) side gets heavy rainfall (Konkan, Malabar coasts). The leeward (eastern) side is a rain shadow — the Deccan Plateau of Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh gets relatively less rainfall (300–700mm).

q: Nagarjunasagar Dam is on:
explain: Nagarjunasagar Dam on the Krishna river (Telangana-Andhra Pradesh border) has one of the world's largest masonry dams. The reservoir provides irrigation and drinking water to both states.

q: The Green Revolution was primarily associated with which crop?
explain: The Green Revolution (mid-1960s) was primarily about wheat — using HYV seeds in Punjab, Haryana, and western UP. M.S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug were key figures. India became self-sufficient in wheat.

q: The Himalayas were formed by the collision of:
explain: The Himalayas are fold mountains formed c. 50 million years ago when the northward-moving Indo-Australian plate collided with the Eurasian plate. The Tethys Sea's sediments were folded up to form the Himalayas (still rising ~5mm/year).

q: Lake Victoria is significant for:
opts: Being the source of the White Nile and Africa's largest lake
Being the deepest lake in Africa
Having the greatest volume of water
explain: Lake Victoria (68,870 sq km) in East Africa (shared by Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya) is Africa's largest lake by area and the source of the White Nile. It is the world's second-largest freshwater lake by area.

q: The Caspian Sea is classified as:
opts: A sea with access to the ocean
A bay of the Indian Ocean
explain: The Caspian Sea (370,000 sq km) is the world's largest lake by surface area — it is a landlocked saltwater/brackish body between Europe and Asia (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan).

q: Which is India's highest waterfall?
explain: Kunchikal Falls (455 m) on the Varahi river in Shimoga/Shivamogga district, Karnataka, is India's highest waterfall. Jog Falls (253 m) on the Sharavathi river is the most famous. Dudhsagar Falls (310 m) is on the Goa-Karnataka border.

q: Tuticorin (Thoothukudi) is known for:
opts: Pearl diving, salt industry, and V.O. Chidambaranar Port
explain: Tuticorin (Thoothukudi) is known for pearl diving (Gulf of Mannar), salt production (India's largest salt-producing area), V.O. Chidambaranar Port (major port), and thermal power plant.

q: The 'time zone' concept was introduced to standardize time because:
opts: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours (15° per hour), causing local times to differ
The sun rises at different times
explain: Earth rotates 15° per hour (360°/24h). For every 15° of longitude, time differs by 1 hour. Time zones standardize this so regions use the same clock time. The 1884 Washington Conference established 24 time zones.

q:
With reference to irrigation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Canal irrigation is the dominant source of irrigation in the alluvial plains of North India.
2. Tank irrigation is historically significant in the Deccan Plateau region, especially Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — canal irrigation dominates the northern alluvial plains, and tank irrigation has long been significant in the hard-rock Deccan region, particularly Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

q: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit global warming to:
explain: The Paris Agreement (COP21, December 2015) aims to hold global average temperature increase to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

q: The Kaveri river originates from which state?
explain: The Kaveri river originates from the Brahmagiri hills in Kodagu (Coorg) district of Karnataka and flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

q: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is related to:
opts: Conservation of wetlands of international importance
explain: The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (signed in Ramsar, Iran, 1971) is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. India has 75 Ramsar sites (as of 2023). Largest: Sundarbans, West Bengal.

q: Which Indian river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
explain: The Damodar River was called the 'Sorrow of Bengal' due to its frequent and devastating floods. Now controlled by the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) dams.

q: The smallest country in the world (by area) is:
explain: Vatican City (0.44 sq km) is the world's smallest country by both area and population. It is an independent city-state within Rome, Italy, and is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church.

q: India's first expressway was:
explain: Ahmedabad-Vadodara Expressway (National Expressway 1) was India's first 6-lane controlled-access expressway, opened in 1998 (partial) and fully in 1999. Mumbai-Pune was the first fully access-controlled expressway.

q: The Damodar river is called 'Sorrow of Bengal' because:
opts: It frequently flooded and caused massive damage
explain: Damodar river was called 'Sorrow of Bengal' for its devastating floods. The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC, 1948) — modeled after Tennessee Valley Authority (USA) — built dams to control floods and generate power.

q: The Equator passes through which continents?
opts: South America, Africa, and Asia (through the islands of Indonesia)
explain: The Equator (0° latitude) passes through 3 continents: South America (Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil), Africa (Gabon, Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia), and Asia (Indonesian islands — Sumatra, Borneo, Sulawesi).

q:
With reference to urbanisation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Maharashtra has one of the highest urban populations in absolute numbers among Indian states.
2. India's level of urbanisation (percentage of population living in urban areas) exceeds 70%, similar to most developed nations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — India's urbanisation level was around 31% as per Census 2011, well below 70%, unlike most developed nations.

q: The Dal Lake is in:
explain: Dal Lake is in Srinagar, J&K. Known for its houseboats and shikaras, it is called the 'Jewel in the Crown of Kashmir'. It has four basins and covers about 18 sq km.

q:
With reference to cropping seasons in India, consider the following statements:
1. Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested in autumn.
2. Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in spring.
3. Rice and wheat are respectively typical Kharif and Rabi crops.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct and are standard NCERT-level facts about India's cropping seasons. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q: The Dibang, Lohit, and Subansiri are tributaries of:
explain: Dibang, Lohit, Subansiri, Siang (Brahmaputra main), and Tista are major tributaries joining the Brahmaputra in Assam. Together they make the Brahmaputra the second-largest river system in India by discharge.

q: Which is the busiest and largest container port of India by volume of container traffic handled?
explain: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva), near Mumbai, is India's largest and busiest container port.

q: The Doab is the land between:
opts: Two rivers (often refers to the Ganga-Yamuna Doab)
explain: 'Doab' (Persian: do = two, ab = water) is the land between two rivers. The Ganga-Yamuna Doab (between Ganga and Yamuna) is the most fertile agricultural land in India. Punjab has five doabs between the five rivers.

q: The term 'Golden Triangle' in Indian tourism refers to:
explain: India's 'Golden Triangle' tourism circuit covers Delhi (Mughal monuments, history), Agra (Taj Mahal), and Jaipur (Pink City, Rajput forts and palaces). It is the most popular tourist circuit in India.

q: Palk Strait separates India from:
explain: Palk Strait is a narrow stretch of water between Tamil Nadu (India) and Northern Sri Lanka. The Adam's Bridge (Ram Sethu) is a chain of natural limestone shoals across the strait.

q: The Kaziranga National Park is on the banks of:
explain: Kaziranga National Park is in Golaghat and Nagaon districts of Assam, on the banks of the Brahmaputra river. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for the one-horned rhinoceros and Bengal tiger.

q: The Atacama Desert in South America (Chile/Peru) is the driest because:
opts: Rain shadow of the Andes plus the cold Humboldt current
explain: Atacama is the world's driest non-polar desert due to: (1) rain shadow of the Andes blocking Atlantic moisture, and (2) cold Humboldt current stabilizing the atmosphere, preventing convective rainfall.

q: The state with the longest coastline in India is:
explain: Gujarat has the longest coastline (1,600+ km) among Indian states, followed by Andhra Pradesh (~974 km) and Tamil Nadu (~906 km). India's total coastline is about 7,517 km (including islands).

q: As per Census 2011, which Indian state recorded the highest sex ratio (females per 1000 males)?
explain: Kerala recorded the highest sex ratio among Indian states in Census 2011, at 1,084 females per 1,000 males.

q: The Chilika Lake (largest coastal lagoon in India) is in:
explain: Chilika Lake in Odisha is India's largest coastal lagoon and one of the world's largest. It is a Ramsar wetland site famous for migratory birds, especially flamingos.

q: The 'Bolan Pass' connects:
explain: Bolan Pass in Pakistan's Balochistan connects the Indus plains (Sindh/Punjab) with Quetta and Afghanistan. Historically, it was one of the main invasion routes into the Indian subcontinent from Central Asia.

q: The Dzukou Valley is in:
explain: Dzukou Valley (2,452 m) on the Nagaland-Manipur border is known as the 'Valley of Flowers of the Northeast' — famous for its seasonal flowers, especially the Dzukou lily. It is a biodiversity-rich valley.

q: The Nile river flows through:
explain: The Nile flows north through eastern Africa — originating in the Ethiopian Highlands (Blue Nile source: Lake Tana) and central Africa (White Nile source: Lake Victoria area) before flowing through Sudan and Egypt into the Mediterranean.

q:
With reference to the Brahmaputra, consider the following statements:
1. It is known as the Tsangpo in Tibet before entering India.
2. It is called the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — the Brahmaputra is called the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet and the Jamuna in Bangladesh (before merging with the Padma/Ganga).

q: The Deccan Plateau is bounded by:
explain: The Deccan Plateau is a large triangular plateau bounded by the Western Ghats (west), Eastern Ghats (east), and Vindhya/Satpura ranges (north). It slopes gently eastward.

q: The Kaveri river originates from:
explain: The Kaveri (Cauvery) river originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu (Coorg) district, Karnataka, at 1341m altitude in the Brahmagiri Hills. It flows ~765 km and empties into the Bay of Bengal near Kaveripattinam.

q: Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary) in Rajasthan is famous for:
explain: Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur, Rajasthan) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous as a winter habitat for migratory birds including the (now rarely seen) Siberian Crane. It has over 370 bird species.

q:
Statement-I: The Godavari is called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South).
Statement-II: It is the longest river of peninsular India and holds major religious/cultural significance comparable to the Ganga in the south.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Both statements are correct, and the Godavari's length and cultural/religious significance (Statement-II) together explain its popular epithet 'Dakshin Ganga' (Statement-I).

q:
Match List-I (demographic indicator) with List-II (Census 2011 leading state) and select the correct answer:

List-I
A. Highest sex ratio
B. Highest literacy rate
C. Lowest population density (among major states)

1. Kerala

explain: Kerala has both the highest sex ratio (1,084) and highest literacy rate; sparsely populated hill/north-eastern states like Arunachal Pradesh have the lowest density; Meghalaya was among states with a very high decadal growth rate in 2001-11. Correct: A-1, B-4, C-2, D-3.

q: Black cotton soil (Regur) is mainly found in:
explain: Black soil (Regur/Black Cotton Soil) covers about 5.46 lakh km² of the Deccan plateau. It is derived from basaltic Deccan Trap rock. Rich in iron, lime, magnesium. Highly moisture-retentive — ideal for cotton. Maharashtra, MP, Karnataka, Gujarat, AP.

q: Which is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean?
explain: The Java Trench (Sunda Trench) at approximately 7,290 m depth is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean, located south of Java (Indonesia). The Mariana Trench is in the Pacific Ocean.

q: Neyveli Lignite (brown coal) is found in:
explain: Neyveli in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu has the largest deposits of lignite (brown coal) in India. NLC India Limited (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation) mines it and generates electricity.

q: Kaziranga National Park (Assam) is known for:
explain: Kaziranga National Park in Assam has the world's largest population of the one-horned Indian rhinoceros (about 2,400 — 70% of the world's population). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: The Godavari is also called:
explain: The Godavari (1465km) is the longest Peninsular river and is called 'Dakshina Ganga' (Ganga of the South) due to its sacred importance. It originates in Nashik, Maharashtra, and flows into the Bay of Bengal through Andhra Pradesh.

q: Which state/UT has the highest literacy rate in India (as per census)?
explain: Kerala consistently has India's highest literacy rate — 96.2% as per 2011 census, and even higher in recent NFHS surveys. Kerala's high literacy is attributed to colonial-era missionary schools and state focus on education.

q: The 'continental shelf' is:
opts: The submerged edge of a continent (to ~200m)
A mountain range under the sea
explain: The continental shelf is the gently sloping submerged extension of a continent from the shoreline to a depth of about 200 m. Beyond it is the steeper continental slope, then the ocean floor/abyssal plain.

q: The Chilika Lake supports livelihoods of how many fishing communities approximately?
explain: About 2 lakh (200,000) fishermen from approximately 150 villages around Chilika Lake depend on it for their livelihoods. The lake's rich aquatic life (fish, prawns, crabs) sustains these communities.

q: Project Elephant was launched in India in:
explain: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 by the Government of India to protect elephant habitats, study elephant populations, and address human-elephant conflict. India has about 60% of the world's Asian elephants.

q: Which Indian State/UT has no international borders?
explain: Maharashtra has no international borders — it is surrounded by Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Karnataka, and Goa, plus the Arabian Sea coast. Border states touch Pakistan, China, Bangladesh, Myanmar, or Nepal/Bhutan.

q: The Deccan Plateau is bounded in the north by:
explain: The Deccan Plateau is bounded by the Vindhya and Satpura Ranges in the north, the Western Ghats in the west, and the Eastern Ghats in the east.

q:
Consider the following statements on the Indian coastline:
1. India has a total coastline of over 7,500 km, including island territories.
2. The western coastal plain is generally narrower than the eastern coastal plain.
3. The eastern coastal plain has well-developed deltas formed by rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi.
4. Backwaters (like those in Kerala) are found exclusively along the eastern coast.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect — Kerala's famous backwaters (e.g., Vembanad Lake) are on the western coast, not the eastern coast. Hence only three.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's geographical extent:
1. India's mainland extends from Kashmir in the north to Kanniyakumari in the south.
2. The Indian Standard Meridian (82°30'E) passes through Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.
3. India's longitudinal extent spans roughly from 68°7'E to 97°25'E.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct standard facts about India's geographical extent and Standard Meridian. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q: The Eastern Ghats are interrupted by which rivers?
explain: Unlike the continuous Western Ghats, the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous (broken/dissected) because major Deccan rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Pennar, Kaveri) cut through them as they flow east to the Bay of Bengal.

q: The National Waterway No. 1 (NW-1) is on:
explain: National Waterway No. 1 (NW-1) is on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Allahabad (Prayagraj) to Haldia (West Bengal), covering 1,620 km. India has 111 national waterways.

q:
Consider the following statements about ecosystem types and their geography:
1. Grassland ecosystems in India include the Terai region and parts of the Deccan.
2. Wetland ecosystems support high biodiversity and act as natural water purifiers.
3. Desert ecosystems have low biodiversity but species are highly adapted to arid conditions.
4. Coral reef ecosystems in India are found only along the mainland coast, never around islands.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect — India's major coral reefs are actually concentrated around island groups (Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar) and the Gulf of Kutch/Mannar, not exclusively the mainland coast. Hence only three.

q:
Statement-I: The Deccan Plateau is triangular in shape and slopes generally from west to east.
Statement-II: Most major peninsular rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri flow eastward and drain into the Bay of Bengal.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II is a consequence of Statement-I (the west-to-east slope), not an explanation for it — the causal direction runs the other way (the slope explains the river flow, not vice versa).

q: The largest country in Africa by area is:
explain: Algeria (2.38 million sq km) is the largest country in Africa by area and the 10th largest in the world, after the 2011 partition of Sudan (which created South Sudan — Sudan is now smaller).

q: The Eastern Coastal Plains of India (between Eastern Ghats and Bay of Bengal) include:
opts: Utkal Plains (Odisha), Andhra Pradesh plains, Tamil Nadu plains (Coromandel)
Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu only
explain: Eastern Coastal Plains stretch from the Mahanadi delta (Odisha) southward through AP to Tamil Nadu's Coromandel Coast. Includes Utkal Plains (Odisha), Andhra coastal plain, and Tamil Nadu's Coromandel Coast.

q: According to the 2011 census, India's population was approximately:
explain: India's population was 1.21 billion (121 crore) as per the 2011 census. India is projected to overtake China as the world's most populous country — which happened around 2023.

q: The Pulicat Lake (Pulicat Bird Sanctuary) is located on the border of:
explain: Pulicat Lake (Pulicat or Pazhaverkadu) is the second largest brackish water lagoon in India, located on the Tamil Nadu-Andhra Pradesh border. It is famous for flamingos and migratory birds. The greater part is in Andhra Pradesh.

q: The Rann of Kutch is a unique geographical feature because:
opts: It is a large salt marsh/seasonal lake (dry in summer, flooded in monsoon)
It is the largest desert in India
explain: The Rann of Kutch (Gujarat) is a large seasonal salt marsh — dry and salty in summer (white expanse), and partially flooded during monsoon. It covers ~23,000 sq km. Famous for the Wild Ass Sanctuary and Rann Utsav.

q: Which Indian river flows westward (into the Arabian Sea) rather than eastward?
explain: The Narmada and Tapti (Tapi) rivers flow westward through the Narmada and Tapti rift valleys and empty into the Arabian Sea (Gulf of Khambhat). Most Peninsular rivers flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

q: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu is famous for:
explain: Vedanthangal (Chengalpattu district) is Asia's oldest and one of India's most important bird sanctuaries. It hosts thousands of migratory and resident water birds during the breeding season (Nov-March). Established c. 1798 by local farmers.

q: The English Channel separates:
explain: The English Channel (La Manche in French) separates southern England from northern France. The Channel Tunnel (Chunnel, 1994) connects the two countries under the sea. The strait is 33 km wide at its narrowest (Dover-Calais).

q: The sex ratio (females per 1000 males) in India as per 2011 census was:
explain: India's sex ratio was 940 females per 1000 males (2011 census), up from 933 (2001). Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1084) and Haryana the lowest (879). Tamil Nadu's sex ratio is 995.

q: The Palk Strait separates India from:
explain: The Palk Strait separates Tamil Nadu in India from the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.

q: The standard meridian of India is:
explain: The standard meridian of India is 82°30'E (passing through Mirzapur, UP), which is used to determine Indian Standard Time (IST = UTC+5:30).

q:
Match List-I (landform) with List-II (formation process) and select the correct answer:

A. Fjord
B. Delta
C. Atoll
D. Rift Valley

q: The longest river in the world is:
explain: The Nile River (Africa) is traditionally considered the longest river at approximately 6,650 km. However, some studies suggest the Amazon may be longer. The Nile flows through Uganda, Sudan, and Egypt into the Mediterranean.

q: The Anamalai Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu is in:
explain: Anamalai Tiger Reserve (Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary) is near Pollachi, Coimbatore district, Tamil Nadu. It covers part of the Anamalai Hills (Western Ghats) shared with Kerala (Parambikulam).

q: The Rann of Kutch is a seasonal salt marsh located in:
explain: The Rann of Kutch is a vast seasonal salt marsh in Gujarat, India, and Pakistan. It is the world's largest salt desert.

q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its history of devastating floods?
explain: The Kosi river, notorious for frequently changing its course and causing severe floods in Bihar, is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

q: The Vaigai river flows through which district's headquarters?
explain: The Vaigai river flows through the heart of Madurai city (Tamil Nadu). It originates in the Varusanadu Hills and drains into the Gulf of Mannar near Ramnad. Major dams: Vaigai dam (Dindigul).

q: The 'Delta' of a river is formed at:
opts: Mouth of the river where it meets the sea
explain: A river delta is a landform created by deposition of sediment carried by a river as it enters a slower-moving body of water (sea, ocean, lake). Named after the Greek letter Delta (Δ) due to its triangular shape.

q: Which Indian state produces the most cotton?
explain: Gujarat is India's largest cotton producer (about 35% of India's cotton). Maharashtra (Vidarbha) is second. India is the world's largest cotton producer. Cotton requires black cotton soil and moderate rainfall.

q:
With reference to biosphere reserves in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, established in 1986, was India's first biosphere reserve.
2. The Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve spans parts of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
3. All Indian biosphere reserves are automatically included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves upon notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — national notification and UNESCO's World Network inclusion are separate steps; not every Indian biosphere reserve is automatically part of the UNESCO network (e.g., Agasthyamalai was notified in 2001 but joined UNESCO's network only in 2016). Hence 1 and 2 only.

q: The 'Dongria Kondh' tribal community opposes mining in:
explain: Dongria Kondh tribe of Niyamgiri Hills (Odisha) successfully opposed Vedanta's bauxite mining project through a historic gram sabha vote in 2013, citing the hills as sacred. Supreme Court upheld their right under Forest Rights Act.

q: Which is the smallest state in India by area?
explain: Goa is the smallest state in India by area (3,702 sq km).

q: The largest ocean in the world is:
explain: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering more than 165 million km² — larger than all land areas combined. It extends from the Arctic to Antarctic.

q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
explain: Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state (approximately 1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh.

q: India's climate is classified as:
explain: India has a tropical monsoon climate (Koppen: Am/Aw/Bsh). The word 'monsoon' comes from Arabic 'mausim' (season). The four seasons: Cold weather (Dec-Feb), Hot weather (Mar-May), Southwest monsoon (Jun-Sep), Retreating monsoon (Oct-Nov).

q: The Pichavaram mangrove forest in Tamil Nadu is between which towns?
explain: Pichavaram mangrove forest is between Chidambaram and Karaikal in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu. It has an area of about 1,100 hectares of mangrove ecosystem along the Bay of Bengal coast.

q: Which Indian state is traditionally the largest producer of coffee?
explain: Karnataka (particularly Kodagu/Coorg and Chikmagalur) is traditionally India's largest coffee-producing state.

q: The Shillong Plateau is in which region of India?
explain: The Shillong Plateau (also called the Meghalaya Plateau) is in Northeastern India, in the state of Meghalaya.

q:
With reference to the Sundarbans, consider the following statements:
1. It is the world's largest mangrove forest, shared between India and Bangladesh.
2. It is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — the Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, shared between India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh, and is a key habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger.

q:
