q: The Son river is a tributary of:
explain: The Son river originates from Amarkantak (MP) — the same plateau as Narmada, but flows north-east to join the Ganga near Patna (Bihar). It is a major right-bank tributary of the Ganga.

q: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
explain: The Sundarbans delta — the world's largest mangrove forest — is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers in West Bengal and Bangladesh.

q: The 'Roaring Forties' refers to:
opts: Strong westerly winds between 40°S and 50°S latitude in the Southern Ocean
explain: The Roaring Forties are powerful westerly winds in the Southern Hemisphere between latitudes 40°–50°S, where there is little land to slow them. They help in navigation of sailing ships (circumnavigation of the globe).

q: The 'Dokar La' Pass and 'Jelep La' Pass are on the border of:
explain: Jelep La Pass (4,270 m) is on the Sikkim-China (Tibet) border and was a major trade route before 1962. Nathu La (4,310 m) is the currently open border crossing between Sikkim and Tibet.

q: Which is the only river that flows from the Deccan Plateau into the Arabian Sea?
explain: Narmada and Tapti (Tapi) are the only two major rivers that flow west from the Deccan Plateau/interior of India and drain into the Arabian Sea. All other major Peninsular rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

q: India's largest solar power plant (as of recent years) is:
opts: Kamuthi Solar Power Project, Tamil Nadu
explain: Bhadla Solar Park in Jodhpur, Rajasthan (~2,245 MW) is one of the world's largest solar parks. Earlier, Kamuthi Solar Power Project in Tamil Nadu (648 MW) held this record when commissioned in 2016.

q: Erode district is known as:
opts: Turmeric City (largest turmeric market in Asia)
explain: Erode is called 'Turmeric City' — it has Asia's largest turmeric market. Erode is also known for cotton textiles (Power loom sector), knitwear, and bhavani silk sarees. Bhavani river flows through the district.

q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are geologically an extension of:
opts: Myanmar's Arakan Yoma mountain range (submarine arc)
explain: Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the visible peaks of an otherwise submerged mountain range — an extension of Myanmar's Arakan Yoma (Rakhine Mountains) folded range, part of the Indo-Burman Ranges.

q: The average annual growth rate of India's population (2001-2011) was:
explain: India's population grew from 1.028 billion (2001) to 1.21 billion (2011), at an average annual growth rate of 1.64%. This was lower than the 1991-2001 rate of 1.93%, showing slowing growth.

q: The Palar river is important for which industry in Tamil Nadu?
explain: The Palar river basin supports the leather tanning industry in Vellore and Kancheepuram districts. The river's water was used for tanning, though pollution has been a major issue. Ambur and Vaniyambadi are leather centers.

q: The river Narmada flows into:
explain: The Narmada (originating from Amarkantak, MP) flows westward through the Vindhya-Satpura rift valley and drains into the Arabian Sea near Bharuch in Gujarat.

q: India is the world's largest producer of:
explain: India is the world's largest producer of milk (Operation Flood, since 1998), pulses (about 24% of world production), and spices. India is also the second-largest producer of rice and wheat.

q: The Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park (Tamil Nadu) is famous for:
opts: Coral reefs, dugongs, sea turtles, and diverse marine life
explain: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park (21 islands between Rameswaram and Tuticorin) is the first marine national park in South and Southeast Asia. Famous for coral reefs, dugongs, sea turtles, sea cucumbers, and 3,600+ species.

q: Which type of rainfall is most common in Tamil Nadu during the northeast monsoon?
explain: Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall during the northeast monsoon (October-December) through orographic (relief) rainfall as winds hit the Eastern Ghats.

q:
With reference to west-flowing rivers of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys between the Vindhya-Satpura ranges.
2. The Narmada originates at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh.
3. Both rivers drain into the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — both rivers drain into the Arabian Sea (Gulf of Khambhat), not the Bay of Bengal. Hence 1 and 2 only.

q: The river Yamuna originates from:
explain: The Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri glacier in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand. It flows southward through Uttarakhand, Haryana, Delhi, and UP before joining the Ganga at Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam).

q: The Western Ghats (Sahyadri) separate:
opts: The narrow coastal plains (Malabar/Konkan coast) from the Deccan Plateau
explain: The Western Ghats run ~1600 km parallel to the west coast of India (Gujarat to Kanyakumari). They separate the narrow Konkan/Malabar coastal plains from the broad Deccan Plateau. They receive heavy rainfall due to the southwest monsoon.

q: The Atal Tunnel (formerly Rohtang Tunnel) connects:
opts: Manali (Kullu) to Lahaul-Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh
explain: Atal Tunnel (9.02 km — world's longest high-altitude road tunnel) connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti Valley, providing all-weather connectivity to previously snow-cut areas. Inaugurated in 2020.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian river valley/multipurpose projects:
1. The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on the Sutlej river.
2. The Hirakud Dam is built on the Mahanadi river.
3. The Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on the Narmada river.
4. The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on the Godavari river.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect — the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on the Krishna river, not the Godavari. Hence only three.

q: The Western Ghats in India is also known as:
explain: The Western Ghats are also called Sahyadri Mountains. They run parallel to the western coast of India.

q: Ozone layer is found in which layer of the atmosphere?
explain: The ozone layer is found in the stratosphere (15-50 km altitude), specifically between 20-30 km. It absorbs harmful UV radiation from the sun. CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) deplete the ozone layer.

q: The highest altitude desert in the world is:
explain: The Ladakh Cold Desert (Leh-Ladakh) and the Tibetan Plateau are among the world's highest altitude desert regions, averaging 3,000-5,000 m elevation with very low precipitation and cold temperatures.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Ganga river system:
1. The Ganga originates from the Gangotri glacier as the Bhagirathi, joined later by the Alaknanda at Devprayag.
2. The Ganga forms the Sundarbans delta, the world's largest delta, jointly with the Brahmaputra.
3. The Ganga is entirely a snow-fed river with no monsoon contribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — the Ganga is both snow-fed and heavily monsoon-fed (rain-fed), with significant seasonal flow variation from monsoon rainfall. Hence 1 and 2 only.

q: Kodaikanal hill station is known for:
opts: Star-shaped lake, shola forests, and pleasant climate
Being highest hill station in South India
explain: Kodaikanal (Princess of Hill Stations) in the Palani Hills, Tamil Nadu, is known for its star-shaped artificial lake, shola forests, grasslands, and pleasant climate. Silver Cascade waterfall is nearby.

q: The Strait of Malacca connects:
opts: Indian Ocean and South China Sea (between Malaysia and Indonesia)
Bay of Bengal and South China Sea
explain: The Strait of Malacca (between Malaysia/Singapore and Sumatra/Indonesia) is one of the world's most important shipping lanes, connecting the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea and Pacific Ocean.

q: The Pichavaram mangrove ecosystem in Tamil Nadu is between which two river systems?
explain: Pichavaram mangrove ecosystem is located between the Vellar estuary (to the north) and the Coleroon (Kollidam, a distributary of Kaveri) estuary (to the south) in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu.

q: The Palk Strait separates:
opts: India and Sri Lanka (between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka)
explain: The Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka. It is about 64–137 km wide. The Gulf of Mannar lies to the south and Palk Bay to the north of the strait.

q: The latitude that divides India roughly into northern and southern halves passes through:
explain: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) passes through the middle of India, dividing it into tropical south and subtropical north.

q: The most populous state in India is:
explain: Uttar Pradesh (population ~200 million, 2011 census) is the most populous state in India, followed by Maharashtra and Bihar.

q: Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is in which district of Tamil Nadu?
explain: Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is the district headquarters of The Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu. Called 'Queen of Hill Stations', it was a summer capital during British India.

q: The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. How many hotspot regions are in the Western Ghats?
explain: The Western Ghats has 8 hotspot clusters recognised by UNESCO (2012) as outstanding examples of biological diversity.

q: The Bering Strait separates:
explain: The Bering Strait (85 km wide) separates Russia (Siberia, Asia) from the USA (Alaska, North America), connecting the Pacific Ocean (Bering Sea) with the Arctic Ocean. A proposed land bridge existed here during ice ages.

q: The Bishnoi community in Rajasthan is known for:
explain: The Bishnoi community (founded by Guru Jambheshwar in 1485) practices conservation of trees (especially khejri) and wildlife (blackbuck, chinkara). In 1730, Amrita Devi and 363 Bishnois sacrificed their lives protecting khejri trees from the Maharaja's men.

q: Hirakud Dam (world's longest earthen dam) is on:
explain: Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi river in Odisha is one of the world's longest earthen dams at 25.8 km. It forms Hirakud reservoir, one of India's largest artificial lakes.

q: The world's largest ocean is:
explain: The Pacific Ocean (165 million sq km) is the world's largest ocean. It contains the Mariana Trench — the deepest point on Earth (11,034 m).

q: The Valley of Flowers National Park is in:
explain: Valley of Flowers National Park in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand (UNESCO World Heritage Site) is famous for endemic alpine flowers. It is near Badrinath. Discovery credited to British mountaineer Frank Smythe (1931).

q:
With reference to 'Mango showers' and 'Nor'westers', consider the following statements:
1. Mango showers are pre-monsoon showers that benefit mango cultivation in Kerala and Karnataka.
2. Nor'westers (Kaal Baisakhi) are pre-monsoon thunderstorms common in West Bengal and Assam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — mango showers occur pre-monsoon in South India, and Nor'westers (Kaal Baisakhi) are pre-monsoon evening thunderstorms typical of eastern India.

q: The Sahara Desert is in:
explain: The Sahara Desert (world's largest hot desert, ~9.2 million sq km) spans North Africa — Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia, Western Sahara.

q: Itanagar is the capital of:
explain: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh. Arunachal Pradesh is India's largest northeastern state by area and borders China, Bhutan, and Myanmar. Its capital Itanagar is named after Ita Fort.

q: Western Disturbances bring winter rainfall to:
opts: North India (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Jammu & Kashmir)
explain: Western Disturbances are cyclonic systems from the Mediterranean Sea that travel eastward, bringing winter rainfall to North India (especially Punjab, Haryana, UP) — beneficial for Rabi crops (wheat).

q: The Coromandel Coast runs along the:
opts: Southeastern coast of India (Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh)
explain: The Coromandel Coast is the southeastern coast of India — from Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu) to Orissa Mahanadi delta, covering Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coastline along the Bay of Bengal.

q: The state with the largest area in India is:
explain: Rajasthan (342,239 sq km) is the largest state by area in India, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. UP is the most populous state.

q: The Sundarbans mangrove forest is located at the delta of which river?
explain: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, located at the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta (India and Bangladesh). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

q: The North-South and East-West Corridor highway project:
opts: Connects Srinagar to Kanyakumari (N-S) and Porbandar to Silchar (E-W)
Links Northeast India to South India
explain: North-South Corridor: Srinagar (J&K) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu) — 4,076 km. East-West Corridor: Porbandar (Gujarat) to Silchar (Assam) — 3,640 km. Together forming the 7,142 km backbone.

q: The 'Loo' winds in North India are:
opts: Hot, dry winds over the north Indian plains (May-June)
explain: 'Loo' winds are hot, dry, dust-laden local winds that blow in the afternoon over the North Indian Plains (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan) in May-June. They can cause heatstroke and death. They result from intense heating of the Thar Desert.

q: The river Brahmaputra is called 'Tsangpo' in:
explain: The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet (China) where it is called Tsangpo (or Yarlung Tsangpo). It enters India at Arunachal Pradesh (called Siang/Dihang), then becomes Brahmaputra in Assam.

q: India's first Biosphere Reserve on marine ecosystem is:
opts: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, Tamil Nadu
explain: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve (10,500 sq km, Tamil Nadu coast) is India's first marine biosphere reserve (1989) and the first in South and Southeast Asia. It covers 21 islands and rich coral reef ecosystems.

q: Which Indian state is the leading producer of bauxite (the primary ore of aluminium)?
explain: Odisha is India's leading producer of bauxite, accounting for the largest share among states.

q: The Nanda Devi National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) is in:
explain: Nanda Devi National Park in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand (surrounding Nanda Devi peak — 7,816 m) and the Valley of Flowers National Park (Uttarakhand) are together a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding major Indian ports:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) is India's largest container port.
2. Kandla (Deendayal) Port is a major port on the Gujarat coast.
3. Visakhapatnam is the deepest natural harbour on India's east coast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct, well-established facts about India's major ports. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q:
With reference to horticulture in India, consider the following statements:
1. India is among the world's largest producers of fruits and vegetables.
2. Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir are notable for apple cultivation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — India ranks among the top global producers of fruits and vegetables, and Himachal Pradesh/J&K are the primary apple-growing regions.

id: geography-154-The 'Loo' is a hot dry w
q: The 'Loo' is a hot dry wind blowing over:
explain: The Loo is a hot, dry, dust-laden wind that blows over the North Indian plains (Rajasthan, UP, Bihar, Punjab, Haryana) during May-June. Temperatures can reach 45-48°C during Loo conditions.

q: India's first nuclear power plant was at:
explain: India's first nuclear power plant — Tarapur Atomic Power Station (TAPS) in Maharashtra — was established in 1969 with US assistance. It has 4 reactors. Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu) has India's first indigenously built reactor.

q: The Khyber Pass connects:
explain: Khyber Pass (3.5 km wide at narrowest) connects Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul (Afghanistan). Historically the most important invasion route into the Indian subcontinent — used by Persians, Greeks, Mughals.

q: Tirupur is famous for:
explain: Tirupur (Tiruppur) in Coimbatore district is India's largest knitwear export hub — called the 'Knit City', 'Knitwear Capital of India', and 'Dollar City' (dollar=forex earnings). It exports cotton knitwear globally.

q: Which river is known as the 'Lifeline of Rajasthan'?
opts: Indira Gandhi Canal (Luni river is the main river)
explain: The Luni river is the only significant river in Rajasthan (drains into Rann of Kutch). But the Indira Gandhi Canal is often called the 'Lifeline of Rajasthan' as it brings water from the Sutlej-Beas to the Thar Desert.

q: The Pir Panjal Range is in:
opts: Jammu & Kashmir (separating Kashmir Valley from Jammu)
explain: The Pir Panjal Range in J&K is the inner Himalayan range that separates the Kashmir Valley (to the north) from the Jammu region (to the south). The Banihal Pass/Tunnel is in the Pir Panjal Range.

q: The 'Elephant Pass' (A9 Highway) in Sri Lanka connects:
opts: Jaffna Peninsula with mainland Sri Lanka
East Sri Lanka with West Sri Lanka
explain: Elephant Pass is a narrow isthmus connecting the Jaffna Peninsula (northernmost part of Sri Lanka) with the mainland of Sri Lanka. The A9 Highway passes through it. It was strategic during the Sri Lanka civil war.

q: The Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC) mines lignite for power generation in:
explain: Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC India Ltd) is located in Cuddalore district (formerly South Arcot), Tamil Nadu. It mines lignite (brown coal) and operates thermal power plants. Neyveli has Asia's largest opencast lignite mines.

q: The soil type best suited for cotton cultivation is:
explain: Black cotton soil (Regur), found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, Karnataka), is ideal for cotton. It is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime. It holds moisture well.

q: The Tamiraparani river (Thamraparni) flows through:
explain: The Tamiraparani (Thamraparni) originates from Agasthiyamalai (Pothigai Hills, Western Ghats) and flows through Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) into the Gulf of Mannar.

q: Which is the only 'river island' national park in India?
opts: Majuli (not exactly) — Dibru-Saikhowa National Park, Assam is on a river island
explain: Majuli in the Brahmaputra river (Assam) is the world's largest river island (875 sq km). It is a major Vaishnavite cultural center. Dibru-Saikhowa National Park (Assam) is also in the Brahmaputra floodplain.

q:
Statement-I: India's population density increased from about 325 persons/sq km in 2001 to about 382 persons/sq km in 2011.
Statement-II: India's total population continued to grow between 2001 and 2011, even as the decadal growth rate itself slowed compared to the previous decade.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Both statements are correct — continued (though slower) absolute population growth (Statement-II) directly explains the rise in density from 325 to 382 persons/sq km (Statement-I).

q: Which ocean current is responsible for the warm climate of Western Europe?
explain: The North Atlantic Drift (an extension of the Gulf Stream) carries warm tropical water to Western Europe, giving it a mild climate despite its high latitude. Without it, Western Europe would be much colder.

q: Chennai Port (Madras Port) was developed as a:
opts: Major artificial (man-made) harbour on the Coromandel Coast
explain: Chennai Port (established 1881) is the second largest artificial port in India (after Jawaharlal Nehru Port, Mumbai) and the largest in the Bay of Bengal. It is one of India's premier ports for container traffic.

q: 'Biodiversity hotspot' criteria requires the area to have:
opts: 1,500+ endemic plant species and lost 70%+ of original habitat
explain: A biodiversity hotspot must meet two criteria: (1) contain at least 1,500 species of endemic vascular plants, and (2) have lost at least 70% of its original habitat. Western Ghats meets both.

q: The world's longest river is:
explain: The Nile (6,650 km) is the world's longest river, flowing through northeastern Africa into the Mediterranean Sea. The Amazon is the largest by volume/discharge.

q: Nilgiris tea from Tamil Nadu is known for:
opts: High-grown tea with a bright, brisk flavor — used in blends
The most expensive tea in India
Being used for green tea only
explain: Nilgiris tea (Tamil Nadu) is grown at 1,000-2,500 m altitude. It is known for its bright, brisk, and fragrant character. Used in blended teas. Ooty is the main center; Kotagiri and Coonoor are also major tea zones.

q: The 'Prime Meridian' passes through:
explain: The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through the Greenwich Observatory in London, UK, established by international agreement in 1884. It divides the Earth into Eastern and Western hemispheres.

q: The 'Thanjavur delta' (Cauvery delta) is called:
explain: The Thanjavur (Tanjore) district and the Kaveri delta region is called the 'Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu' due to extensive paddy cultivation. It has a well-developed canal irrigation network from the Kaveri river.

q: Which is the largest state in India by area?
explain: Rajasthan is the largest state in India by area (342,239 sq km), followed by Madhya Pradesh.

q: The Suez Canal connects:
explain: The Suez Canal (193 km, Egypt) connects the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea. Opened in 1869, it allows ships to travel between Europe and Asia without going around Africa, reducing the journey by ~7,000 km.

q: The Shillong Plateau (Meghalaya Plateau) is a part of:
opts: The ancient Gondwana landmass (Peninsular India extension)
explain: The Shillong/Meghalaya Plateau is a northeastern extension of the ancient Peninsular (Gondwana) block, separated from the main plateau by the Brahmaputra-Ganga alluvial plains. It is geologically very old.

q: The Cauvery river's major left-bank tributaries include:
explain: Cauvery's major left-bank tributaries in Karnataka are Hemavati, Shimsha, and Arkavathi. In Tamil Nadu, right-bank tributaries include Bhavani, Noyyal, and Amaravathi. Total basin area: ~81,000 sq km.

q: The Mullaperiyar dam is disputed between:
explain: Mullaperiyar dam (built 1895 by British) is in Kerala but owned and operated by Tamil Nadu for irrigation. The dispute is over the dam's safety and water level — Kerala wants a new dam; Tamil Nadu wants the old one maintained.

q: The 'Walker Circulation' is directly related to which climate phenomenon?
explain: Walker Circulation is an atmospheric circulation pattern over the tropical Pacific Ocean. Disruption of Walker Circulation is central to the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon.

q: The highest peak in the Western Ghats is:
explain: Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anamalai Hills of Kerala is the highest peak in the Western Ghats and also the highest peak in South India outside the Himalayas.

q: The Palar river flows through:
opts: Vellore and Kancheepuram districts into Bay of Bengal
explain: The Palar river flows through Vellore and Kancheepuram districts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh before draining into the Bay of Bengal near Mahabalipuram. Vellore and Kancheepuram are major cities on its banks.

q: OPEC (Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries) headquarters is in:
explain: OPEC is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. Founded in Baghdad in 1960, it currently has 13 member countries. Saudi Arabia is the de facto leader. OPEC controls about 40% of world oil production.

q: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) is in which district?
explain: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) is in Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu. It was a major Pallava port city and is UNESCO World Heritage Site for its 7th-8th century rock-cut temples, Shore Temple, and Five Rathas.

q:
With reference to Indian states and Union Territories, consider the following statements:
1. Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, becoming India's newest state at that time.
2. Ladakh became a separate Union Territory in 2019, carved out of Jammu & Kashmir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — Telangana was formed in 2014 from Andhra Pradesh, and Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019 following the reorganisation of Jammu & Kashmir.

q: The Luni river drains into:
opts: Rajasthan desert (dry up before reaching sea)
explain: Luni (320 km) originates from Aravalli Range near Ajmer (Rajasthan) and drains into the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat — making it an endorheic river (no outlet to ocean). Water becomes brackish/saline in lower reaches.

q: The river Brahmaputra enters India from:
explain: The Brahmaputra (called Tsangpo in Tibet) originates in Tibet, China, and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.

q: The Koppen Climate Classification system classifies most of South India as:
explain: Most of the interior peninsular India has Tropical Wet and Dry (Aw — Savanna) climate, with a distinct dry season.

q: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary (Tamil Nadu) is in:
explain: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary in Chengalpattu district, Tamil Nadu, is one of India's oldest bird sanctuaries (1936). It is a winter habitat for migratory birds like painted storks and open-billed storks.

q: The 'Intertropical Convergence Zone' (ITCZ) is:
opts: A line where tropical cyclones form
Where northeast and southeast trade winds converge near the equator — area of low pressure and heavy rainfall
A boundary between troposphere and stratosphere
explain: ITCZ is a belt of low pressure near the equator where NE trade winds (NH) and SE trade winds (SH) converge. The convergence causes air to rise, creating heavy convective rainfall (tropical rainforests). The ITCZ migrates seasonally — in summer it shifts north, driving Indian monsoon.

q:
Consider the following statements on India's demographic transition:
1. India is generally considered to be in the third/later stage of the demographic transition model, with declining birth and death rates.
2. The total fertility rate (TFR) in India has been declining over recent decades.
3. India's death rate has historically declined faster than its birth rate, contributing to rapid population growth in the 20th century.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct and reflect standard demographic transition theory applied to India's population history. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q: The Konkan Railway runs along:
opts: Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka coasts (Mumbai to Mangalore)
East Coast from Chennai to Odisha
explain: Konkan Railway (760 km) was built 1990-1998 along the western coast through Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka, connecting Roha (near Mumbai) to Mangalore. It passes through 2,000+ bridges and 91 tunnels.

q: Which Indian city has the largest natural harbour?
explain: Mumbai (Bombay) has one of the best natural harbours in the world. This is a key reason why it became India's commercial capital — it allowed large ships to dock safely. Vizag is India's deepest port.

q: SAARC headquarters is in:
explain: SAARC Secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal. Founded in 1985, SAARC has 8 members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka.

q: The highest peak within India's undisputed territory is:
explain: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) on the Sikkim-Nepal border is the highest peak within India's undisputed territory. K2 (8,611 m) is higher but lies in POK (disputed). World's third-highest mountain.

q: The 'Roaring Forties', 'Furious Fifties', and 'Screaming Sixties' are associated with:
opts: Strong westerly winds in southern hemisphere
explain: These are strong westerly winds that blow in the southern hemisphere between 40°-70°S latitude. They are unimpeded by land masses and are very strong.

q: Chilika Lake is located in:
explain: Chilika Lake (1,100 sq km) in Odisha is India's largest coastal lagoon and Asia's largest brackish water lake. It is a Ramsar wetland site famous for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins.

q: India's largest river island is:
explain: Majuli in Assam is India's largest river island, located on the Brahmaputra river. It is also the world's largest inhabited river island.

q: The first National Park in India is:
explain: Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand) was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park — India's and Asia's first national park. Renamed Jim Corbett in 1957 and became the first Project Tiger reserve in 1973.

q: Pink Revolution is associated with:
explain: Pink Revolution primarily refers to the increased production of meat (mutton, poultry) in India. Some sources also use it for prawn/shrimp farming or onion production. The colour analogy follows other agricultural revolutions.

q: The Palani hills and Kodaikanal are in:
explain: Palani Hills (part of Western Ghats) and Kodaikanal hill station are in Dindigul district, Tamil Nadu. The hills also extend into Coimbatore and Theni districts.

q: The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) is chaired by:
opts: Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
explain: The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) is chaired by the Prime Minister. It is the apex body for wildlife conservation in India and reviews/approves projects in or near wildlife sanctuaries and national parks.

q: India's National River is:
explain: The Ganga was declared India's National River in 2008 by the government. The National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA) was created for its conservation. The Ganga is also the most sacred river in Hinduism.

q: Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) and Indian Standard Time (IST) differ by:
explain: Indian Standard Time (IST) = GMT + 5 hours 30 minutes (+5:30). India does not observe Daylight Saving Time. IST is based on 82.5°E longitude passing through Mirzapur, UP.

q: 'Laterite soil' is found mainly in:
explain: Laterite soil forms in high-rainfall tropical areas where leaching removes silica, leaving iron and aluminum oxides — giving a reddish colour. Found in Western Ghats, parts of Assam, Karnataka, and Meghalaya.

q: The wettest place in India (and one of the wettest in the world) is:
explain: Mawsynram (11,873mm/year average) and Cherrapunji/Sohra (11,777mm/year) in Meghalaya receive the highest rainfall in India and among the highest in the world. This is due to orographic (relief) rainfall as moist Bay of Bengal winds hit the Khasi Hills.

q: The Kanyakumari district (southernmost in Tamil Nadu) borders:
opts: Kerala, and the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean
explain: Kanyakumari district borders Kerala (Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam districts) on the north-northwest, Tirunelveli district on the north-east, and is surrounded by the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean to the south.

q: The 'Nilgiri Tahr' (Nilgiris Wild Goat) is found:
opts: In the Nilgiri Hills and adjacent Western Ghats
explain: The Nilgiri Tahr (Nilgiris Ibex, Hemitragus hylocrius) is an ungulate endemic to the Nilgiri Hills and adjacent Western Ghats (Tamil Nadu and Kerala). It is found above 1,200m altitude. Eravikulam NP (Kerala) has the largest population.

q: Jute is mainly produced in:
opts: West Bengal (India's leading jute state) and Bangladesh
explain: West Bengal is the leading jute producer in India (about 75% of India's jute). Assam and Bihar also produce jute. Bangladesh is the largest global producer. Jute is called 'Golden Fibre'.

q: The Chilika Lake in Odisha is famous for being the habitat of:
explain: Chilika Lake is Asia's largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar site, famous for migratory birds in winter and Irrawaddy dolphins.

q: Which of these cities is at the highest altitude?
explain: Shimla, the capital of Himachal Pradesh, is at an altitude of about 2,206 meters (7,238 feet), the highest among these cities.

q: The world's largest hot desert (Sahara) is in North Africa. The world's largest cold desert is:
explain: Antarctica is the world's largest cold desert (14.2 million sq km) — it receives very little precipitation. The Gobi Desert in Asia is the world's largest cold desert outside polar regions.

q: Which is the capital of Tamil Nadu?
explain: Chennai (formerly Madras) is the capital of Tamil Nadu and the fourth largest metropolitan city in India.

q: El Niño phenomenon is associated with:
opts: Unusual warming of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean
explain: El Niño is a climate pattern where the central and eastern Pacific Ocean warms unusually, disrupting global weather. It typically causes drought in India (weak monsoon), flooding in South America, and other global effects.

q: The Panama Canal connects:
opts: Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean Sea
explain: The Panama Canal (82 km, Panama) connects the Atlantic (via Caribbean Sea) and Pacific Ocean. Opened in 1914, ships avoid going around South America (Cape Horn), saving about 12,000 km.

q: The longest National Highway in India is:
explain: NH-44 (formerly NH-7) from Srinagar (J&K) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu) is the longest National Highway in India at approximately 3,745 km. It passes through Pathankot, Jalandhar, Delhi, Agra, Nagpur, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, and Madurai.

q: The highest plateau in the world is:
explain: The Tibetan Plateau (average elevation ~4,500 m) is the world's highest and largest plateau, often called the 'Roof of the World'.

q: Chandigarh is the capital of:
opts: Punjab and Haryana both (and a Union Territory itself)
explain: Chandigarh is a Union Territory that serves as the shared capital of both Punjab and Haryana. Designed by Le Corbusier, it was established after Partition (Lahore went to Pakistan) as Punjab's new capital.

q: The capital of Brazil is:
explain: Brasília is the capital of Brazil — a planned capital built in just 41 months and inaugurated in 1960. Before Brasília, Rio de Janeiro was the capital. São Paulo is Brazil's largest city and economic center.

id: geography-529-The Ring of Fire is a zo
q: The Ring of Fire is a zone of:
opts: Volcanoes and earthquakes surrounding the Pacific Ocean
Volcanic activity in the Indian Ocean
explain: The Ring of Fire is a horseshoe-shaped zone of volcanic activity and earthquakes around the Pacific Ocean rim. It has 75% of the world's active volcanoes and experiences 90% of the world's earthquakes.

id: geography-188-The Bhavani river is a t
q: The Bhavani river is a tributary of:
explain: The Bhavani river is a major left-bank tributary of the Kaveri (Cauvery). Bhavani Sagar dam provides water for Erode and Coimbatore districts. The river flows through the Nilgiris and Erode districts.

q: Kanchenjunga, the third-highest peak in the world, is located on the border of India and which country?
explain: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the border between India (Sikkim) and Nepal.

q: The latitude 23.5°N is called the Tropic of Cancer. India's southernmost mainland point Kanyakumari is at approximately:
explain: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin), India's southernmost mainland point, is at 8°4'N. The southernmost point of India's territory (including islands) is Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island at about 6°45'N.

q: Mawsynram (Meghalaya) is famous for:
explain: Mawsynram in Meghalaya receives about 11,872 mm annually — the highest in the world. Cherrapunji (Sohra), nearby, also holds many rainfall records. Both are on the Shillong Plateau facing the Bay of Bengal.

q: The Western Ghats are also known as:
explain: The Western Ghats are also called Sahyadri mountains. They run parallel to India's western coast for 1,600 km through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: India's largest iron ore reserves are in:
opts: Jharkhand and Odisha (Jharkhand-Odisha iron ore belt)
explain: The Jharkhand-Odisha iron ore belt (Singhbhum, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj) has India's largest iron ore reserves. Other important areas: Karnataka (Bellary, Sandur), Chhattisgarh (Bastar), Goa. India has ~5.5 billion tonnes of iron ore reserves.

q: The Malabar Coast is along:
opts: Kerala and coastal Karnataka (Arabian Sea coast)
explain: The Malabar Coast is the southwestern coast of India — specifically Kerala and southern Karnataka along the Arabian Sea. It is known for spice trade, backwaters, and heavy rainfall from southwest monsoon.

q: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located in:
explain: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) — the principal judicial organ of the United Nations — is located in The Hague, Netherlands, in the Peace Palace. It settles disputes between countries.

q: The 'Chipko Movement' was related to:
explain: The Chipko Movement (1973) in Uttarakhand was a nonviolent protest where villagers (led by Sundarlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt) hugged trees to prevent logging. It influenced India's forest policy.

id: geography-114-Red and yellow soil is p
q: Red and yellow soil is predominant in:
opts: Eastern Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand
explain: Red and Yellow soils (formed from ancient crystalline/metamorphic rocks under oxidation) are found in eastern Tamil Nadu (non-Cauvery delta areas), Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, western Andhra Pradesh. Red colour from iron oxide.

q:
Consider the following statements on India's transport network:
1. Roadways carry a larger share of freight and passenger traffic than railways in India today.
2. The Golden Quadrilateral was developed under the National Highways Development Project.
3. Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were developed as integrated steel plant towns aided by rail connectivity.
4. India has no significant coastal shipping network due to its limited coastline.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect — India has a long coastline (over 7,500 km) with a significant, if underutilised, coastal shipping network. Hence only three.

q: India's pharmaceutical hub (largest generic drug exporter) is:
explain: Hyderabad is India's top pharmaceutical hub ('Pharma City'), home to Dr. Reddy's, Cipla, Hetero, Aurobindo, Natco. India is the world's largest exporter of generic medicines.

q: The Great Wall of China was built mainly to:
opts: Protect China from northern nomadic invasions
explain: The Great Wall of China (built/rebuilt over many dynasties, mainly Ming dynasty 1368-1644) was built to protect the Chinese empire from northern nomadic raids (Mongols, Xiongnu). Total length: ~21,196 km.

q: The Barren Island (Andaman) is India's only:
explain: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only active volcano and the only confirmed active volcano in South Asia. It last erupted in 2017 and has been periodically active since its major eruption in 1991.

q: India's Silicon Valley is:
explain: Bengaluru (Bangalore) is called India's Silicon Valley due to concentration of IT companies — Infosys, Wipro, HAL, ISRO are headquartered here. It is also called the 'Pub Capital', 'Garden City', 'Startup Capital of India'.

q: Banihal Pass is the route to:
explain: Banihal Pass (2,832 m) in J&K connects Jammu with the Kashmir Valley. The Banihal Tunnel (Jawahar Tunnel, 2.5 km) provides an all-weather road link. The Banihal-Qazigund rail tunnel is the longest in India.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Green Revolution in India:
1. It involved the adoption of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers and assured irrigation.
2. Its impact was most pronounced in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
3. It led to significant yield gains primarily in wheat and rice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct and standard, well-documented features of India's Green Revolution (from the late 1960s). Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q: The Ganges river enters Bangladesh as:
explain: The Ganga enters Bangladesh at Rajshahi district as the Padma. The Brahmaputra enters Bangladesh as the Jamuna. They join to form the Padma, which then joins the Meghna before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

q: The largest salt lake in India is:
explain: Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan) is India's largest inland saltwater lake (about 230 sq km during monsoon, much smaller in summer). It supplies most of Rajasthan's salt. Chilika is brackish, not fully saline.

q: The river Vaigai flows through:
opts: Madurai and Ramanathapuram — emptying into Palk Bay
explain: The Vaigai river originates in the Varushanad Hills (Dindigul), flows through Madurai, Sivaganga, and Ramanathapuram before emptying into the Palk Bay. It is a significant river in southern Tamil Nadu with the Vaigai Dam at Vaigai.

q: Which continent is India a part of?
explain: India is located in South Asia, which is a subregion of Asia.

q: The Chennai Port is located on:
explain: Chennai Port (formerly Madras Port) is on the east coast of India, on the Bay of Bengal. It is India's second largest port by capacity. It handles 80% of Tamil Nadu's export-import trade.

q: The Deccan Trap region (Deccan Plateau lava flows) consists of:
opts: Basaltic lava rocks — basis for black cotton soil
explain: The Deccan Traps (covering Maharashtra, Gujarat, parts of AP, Karnataka) consist of basaltic lava flows from massive volcanic activity ~66 million years ago (Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary). Weathering of basalt produces black cotton soil.

q: Mawsynram, often cited as one of the wettest places on Earth, is located in which Indian state?
explain: Mawsynram, near Cherrapunji, is located in Meghalaya and receives extremely high annual rainfall due to orographic effect.

q: The Montreal Protocol (1987) aimed to phase out:
opts: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) that deplete the ozone layer
explain: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer (1987) is a landmark treaty phasing out CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) and other ozone-depleting substances. It is considered the most successful environmental treaty.

q: The 'Bhabar' zone, found at the base of the Himalayas, is characterized by:
opts: Porous, coarse sediment where streams disappear underground
explain: Bhabar is a narrow belt (8–16 km wide) at the foothills of Himalayas made of porous gravel and boulders. Streams flowing from hills disappear underground here. South of Bhabar is Terai (waterlogged, where streams re-emerge).

q: The 'Hot Spot' biodiversity theory was developed by which scientist?
explain: The concept of biodiversity hotspots was developed by British ecologist Norman Myers in 1988. Hotspots are areas with exceptional concentrations of endemic species under threat.

q: India's first metro rail was built in:
explain: Kolkata Metro (North-South corridor) is India's first metro rail system, inaugurated on 24 October 1984 (partial). It was the first underground rapid transit system in India. Delhi Metro (2002) is the largest metro network.

q: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway (UNESCO World Heritage) runs between:
explain: Nilgiri Mountain Railway (NMR, built 1908) runs from Mettupalayam (Tamil Nadu foothills) to Ooty (46 km). It uses a unique rack-and-pinion system for the steep climb. Part of 'Mountain Railways of India' UNESCO site.

q: The 'Pichavaram Mangrove Forest' in Tamil Nadu is located near:
explain: Pichavaram Mangrove Forest (1100 hectares) is located near Chidambaram (Cuddalore district), Tamil Nadu. It is one of the world's largest mangrove forests and lies between two estuaries (Vellar and Coleroon/Kollidam rivers).

q: Which state has the highest population density in India (Census 2011)?
explain: Bihar had the highest population density of 1102 persons/km² in Census 2011. West Bengal was second (1029/km²). Among Union Territories, Delhi has the highest density. Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest (17/km²).

q: The North-East monsoon (retreating monsoon) gives rainfall mainly to:
opts: Tamil Nadu coast and Andhra Pradesh
explain: Tamil Nadu and coastal Andhra Pradesh receive most of their rainfall from the Northeast monsoon (October–December) when it blows from the Bay of Bengal, picking moisture and depositing it on the Coromandel coast. Tamil Nadu gets 60% of its rainfall from this monsoon.

q: The Papanasam (Aazhiyar) dam in Tamil Nadu is on:
explain: Papanasam (Aazhiyar) dam is on the Tamiraparani river in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu. Shengottai-Papanasam area is known for the Courtallam (Kutralam) waterfalls fed by the Chittar river.

q: The Snow Leopard is found in:
explain: Snow Leopard is found in the high-altitude zones of the Himalayas and Karakoram in J&K, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand. India has about 400-700 snow leopards. It is Classified as Vulnerable by IUCN.

q: The southwest monsoon arrives in India first in:
explain: The southwest monsoon arrives in Kerala around 1 June each year and then progresses northward. Kerala is the first Indian State to receive the southwest monsoon.

q: The Palk Bay lies between:
opts: Tamil Nadu coast and the Palk Strait to the east
India and Sri Lanka on all sides
explain: The Palk Bay is a shallow bay bounded by Tamil Nadu on the west, the Palk Strait on the east (between India and Sri Lanka), and Rameshwaram/Pamban Island on the south. Fishing is important here.

q:
Statement-I: Tamil Nadu receives a significant share of its annual rainfall from the north-east (retreating) monsoon rather than the south-west monsoon.
Statement-II: The Western Ghats block the south-west monsoon winds from directly reaching Tamil Nadu's east coast, leaving it comparatively drier during that season and dependent instead on the north-east monsoon.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Both statements are correct, and the rain-shadow effect of the Western Ghats described in Statement-II is precisely why Tamil Nadu depends more on the north-east monsoon, as stated in Statement-I.

q: Tamil Nadu shares its longest border with which State?
explain: Tamil Nadu shares borders with Andhra Pradesh (northeast), Karnataka (north-northwest), and Kerala (west). The border with Andhra Pradesh is the longest.

q: The southernmost tip of mainland India is:
explain: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin), Tamil Nadu is the southernmost tip of peninsular (mainland) India. Indira Point in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands is the southernmost point of Indian territory overall.

q: The Tungabhadra Dam (supporting Vijayanagara area) is in:
explain: Tungabhadra Dam is in Hospet, Karnataka on the Tungabhadra river (a tributary of Krishna). It provides irrigation water to Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. The Hampi (Vijayanagara) ruins are nearby.

q: The 'Bhabar' zone at the foothills of the Himalayas is characterized by:
explain: The Bhabar is a narrow belt (8-16 km wide) at the foot of the Shivalik Hills (outer Himalayas). It consists of porous, coarse gravel deposits where streams lose themselves underground. South of Bhabar is the Terai (marshy zone).

q: 'Lagoons' are:
opts: Coastal water bodies separated from the sea by a sandbar
explain: Lagoons are shallow water bodies (lakes) separated from the larger sea/ocean by a narrow barrier of land (sandbar, barrier island, or coral reef). Chilika (Odisha) and Pulicat (Tamil Nadu-AP) are famous Indian lagoons.

q:
With reference to inland waterways and river linking, consider the following statements:
1. National Waterway 1 runs along the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system.
2. The Ken-Betwa Link is one of India's river-interlinking projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — NW-1 runs on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly stretch, and the Ken-Betwa Link is a real, prominent river-interlinking project.

q: The Sathankulam-Koonthankulam Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu is famous for:
opts: Spot-billed pelicans and migratory water birds
explain: Koonthankulam Bird Sanctuary in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu is one of the largest bird sanctuaries in Asia, famous for the spot-billed pelican (Pelecanus philippensis) and other migratory water birds.

q: India shares its longest international border with which country?
explain: India shares its longest international border with Bangladesh (4,096 km).

q: ISRO's satellite launch center (SDSC-SHAR) is at:
explain: ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) is at Sriharikota island on Pulicat Lake, in Andhra Pradesh. It is India's main satellite launch center. ISRO's HQ and research centers are in Bengaluru.

q: The capital of Japan is:
explain: Tokyo is the capital and largest city of Japan (population ~14 million city, ~38 million metro area — world's largest metropolitan area). Before 1868, Kyoto was Japan's capital.

q: The rain shadow area of Western Ghats leads to dry conditions in:
opts: Eastern Maharashtra, northern Karnataka, and Rayalaseema
explain: The rain shadow region (leeward side) of the Western Ghats is in eastern Maharashtra (Marathwada, Vidarbha), Bidar (Karnataka), and Rayalaseema (AP) — these areas receive much less rainfall and face drought.

id: geography-457-What is the capital of T
q: What is the capital of Tamil Nadu's Nilgiri district?
explain: Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is the district headquarters of the Nilgiri district in Tamil Nadu, and a popular hill station.

q: The Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project aims to:
opts: Create a navigable channel through the Palk Strait (Adams Bridge area)
Build a bridge between India and Sri Lanka
explain: Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project proposes to dredge a channel through the Palk Strait and Palk Bay (along the Adam's Bridge alignment) to enable ships to pass through, avoiding the longer route around Sri Lanka.

id: geography-384-The Chenab river is a tr
q: The Chenab river is a tributary of:
explain: Chenab is the largest of the five Punjab rivers. It originates from the Lahaul Valley (Himachal Pradesh), flows through J&K and Pakistan, and joins the Indus through the Panjnad (confluence of five rivers).

q: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) was related to:
explain: The Kyoto Protocol (1997, entered force 2005) was the first binding international agreement on greenhouse gas emission reductions. It set targets for developed countries. USA never ratified it.

q:
Match List-I (mountain pass) with List-II (location/state) and select the correct answer:

List-I
A. Nathu La
B. Zoji La
C. Palghat Gap
D. Bomdi La

List-II
1. Jammu & Kashmir/Ladakh
2. Kerala-Tamil Nadu (Western Ghats)
3. Sikkim
4. Arunachal Pradesh
explain: Nathu La is in Sikkim (India-China border); Zoji La connects Kashmir Valley to Ladakh; Palghat Gap is the well-known break in the Western Ghats between Kerala and Tamil Nadu; Bomdi La is in Arunachal Pradesh. Correct: A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

q: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) headquarters is in:
explain: NATO's political headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium (moved from Paris in 1967). Its military headquarters (Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe — SHAPE) is in Mons, Belgium.

q:
Consider the following statements about India's neighbouring countries and border lengths:
1. India shares its longest land border with Bangladesh.
2. The Radcliffe Line demarcates the India-Pakistan border in Punjab/Rajasthan, and also parts of the India-Bangladesh border.
3. The McMahon Line demarcates part of the India-China border in the eastern sector.
4. India shares a land border with exactly three countries in total.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect — India shares land borders with seven countries (Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Afghanistan via PoK), not three. Hence only three.

q: The Krishna river originates from:
explain: The Krishna (1,400 km) originates from Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra's Western Ghats. It flows east through Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh, draining into the Bay of Bengal. Nagarjunasagar dam is on it.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the world's major deserts:
1. The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert.
2. The Gobi Desert is a cold desert located in Central Asia.
3. The Atacama Desert in South America is among the driest places on Earth.
4. All deserts are located within the tropics.
How many of the above statements are correct?
explain: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect — deserts also occur in temperate and cold regions (e.g., Gobi, Patagonian, polar deserts), not confined to the tropics. Hence only three.

q: The Ganga Action Plan was launched to:
opts: Clean and rejuvenate the polluted Ganga river (1986)
explain: Ganga Action Plan (GAP) was launched in 1986 by PM Rajiv Gandhi to address pollution of the Ganga. Currently, the Namami Gange Programme (2015) is the comprehensive mission to clean and revitalize the Ganga.

q: The Konkan Coast is the western coastal strip of:
explain: The Konkan Coast is the narrow coastal strip between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, primarily covering Maharashtra (south of Mumbai) and Goa. It is known for alphonso mangoes, cashews, and coconuts.

q: The 'Indian Standard Time' meridian (82.5°E) passes through:
explain: The IST meridian (82.5°E longitude) passes through Mirzapur/Naini near Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh. India is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT (UTC+5:30).

q: The Narmada river flows into which sea?
explain: The Narmada (also Narmadā) is a westward-flowing river that drains into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay). Most rivers of the Deccan Plateau flow eastward to the Bay of Bengal.

q: The Dead Sea (Israel/Jordan border) is famous for:
opts: Being the lowest point on Earth's land surface and extreme salinity
explain: The Dead Sea (430 m below sea level) is the lowest point on Earth's land surface. Its salinity is about 34% (10 times the ocean), making it impossible for most aquatic life to survive — hence 'Dead' Sea.

q: The Kalpakkam Nuclear Power Plant (Tamil Nadu) is significant because:
opts: India's first indigenously built nuclear reactor (MAPS)
explain: Kalpakkam (Madras Atomic Power Station — MAPS) houses India's first indigenously designed and built nuclear reactor. India's Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR, 1985) and Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) are also here.

q: The Thar Desert is located in which state?
explain: The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) is mainly in Rajasthan. It extends into parts of Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana as well.

q: Pichavaram in Tamil Nadu is famous for:
opts: Second largest mangrove forest in the world
explain: Pichavaram near Chidambaram (Cuddalore district) has one of the world's largest mangrove forests (~1,100 ha). It is a rich ecosystem and a popular eco-tourism spot in Tamil Nadu.

q: The McMahon Line is the boundary between:
explain: The McMahon Line (1914, Simla Convention) is the disputed boundary between India and China (Tibet) in the northeastern Himalayas. China does not recognize this line; it claims Arunachal Pradesh as 'South Tibet'.

q: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa, is located in which country?
explain: Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m), Africa's highest peak, is located in Tanzania, near the border with Kenya.

q: The easternmost point of India is:
explain: Kibithu in Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh (97.5°E) is the easternmost village/point of India. India's easternmost extent is about 97°25'E longitude.

q: Which is the largest river in the world by water volume?
explain: The Amazon River in South America carries the greatest volume of water of any river in the world.

q: The Himalayan range is classified as:
explain: The Himalayas are fold mountains, formed when the Indian tectonic plate collided with the Eurasian plate (~50 million years ago), folding sedimentary rocks upward. They are still rising about 5 mm per year.

q: The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) is headquartered in:
explain: IMD (India Meteorological Department) is headquartered in Pune, Maharashtra (Shivajinagar). It was established in 1875 and is the principal government agency for weather forecasting and seismology.

q:
With reference to petroleum resources in India, consider the following statements:
1. Mumbai High is a major offshore oilfield in the Arabian Sea.
2. Digboi in Assam was the site of India's first oil well.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct — Mumbai High is a major offshore field, and Digboi (Assam) hosted India's first oil well and refinery, dating to the late 19th century.

q: National Highway 48 (old NH-8) connects:
explain: NH-48 (formerly NH-8) is one of India's busiest highways, connecting Delhi to Mumbai (via Gurugram, Jaipur, Ajmer, Udaipur, Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat). Part of the Golden Quadrilateral.

q: The Atacama Desert — the driest place on Earth — is in which continent?
explain: The Atacama Desert, the driest non-polar desert on Earth, is in northern Chile (South America).

q:
Consider the following statements regarding ocean currents:
1. The Gulf Stream is a warm current that moderates the climate of Western Europe.
2. The Humboldt (Peru) Current is a cold current flowing along the western coast of South America.
3. Ocean currents in the Northern Hemisphere generally move clockwise due to the Coriolis effect.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct standard oceanography facts covered in physical geography. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q: Which geographical phenomenon explains why there is a 'dry port' in Rajasthan despite being far from sea?
explain: Rajasthan's Aravalli range acts as a barrier, blocking the southwest monsoon from penetrating the Thar Desert, making it extremely arid.

q: The Radcliffe Line is the border between:
explain: The Radcliffe Line (drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947) is the boundary between India and Pakistan, and between India and (East) Bangladesh. It was drawn in 5 weeks and announced on 17 August 1947.

q: The Mahanadi river delta (rice bowl of Odisha) drains into:
opts: Bay of Bengal near Cuttack/Bhubaneswar coast
explain: The Mahanadi (925 km) originates from Chhattisgarh and drains into the Bay of Bengal, forming a large delta in coastal Odisha. The delta region produces substantial rice. Hirakud dam is on the Mahanadi.

q: The Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur was built by:
explain: Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajarajeswarar Temple) was built by Rajaraja Chola I and consecrated in 1010 CE. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva, stands 66 m tall, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Which type of vegetation is found in the Nilgiri hills (Tamil Nadu)?
explain: Shola forests are a type of subtropical montane forest found in the Nilgiri, Anamalai, and Palani hills. They are isolated patches of stunted trees in valley bottoms, interspersed with grasslands on higher slopes. Unique biodiversity hotspot.

q:
Match List-I (crop) with List-II (leading Indian producing state) and select the correct answer:

List-I
A. Sugarcane
B. Cotton
C. Tea
D. Jute

List-II
1. West Bengal (leading raw jute producer)
2. Uttar Pradesh (leading sugarcane producer)
3. Gujarat (leading cotton producer)
4. Assam (leading tea producer)
explain: Uttar Pradesh leads sugarcane; Gujarat leads cotton; Assam leads tea; West Bengal leads raw jute. Correct: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

q: Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall from:
explain: Tamil Nadu is unique — it receives about 60% of its annual rainfall from the Northeast (Retreating) monsoon during October-December. This is why Tamil Nadu gets rain when most other states have post-monsoon dry weather.

q: The Aravalli Range runs through:
explain: The Aravalli Range (about 800 km) runs from Gujarat (Palanpur) through Rajasthan to Delhi-Haryana border. It is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world. Mount Abu (1,722 m) is the highest peak.

q:
Consider the following statements about forest resources in India:
1. Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover by area among Indian states.
2. Mizoram has among the highest forest cover as a percentage of its geographical area.
3. Tropical evergreen forests are predominantly found in regions of very high rainfall like the Western Ghats and North-East India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct — per India State of Forest Report data, MP leads in absolute forest area, Mizoram leads in forest-cover percentage, and tropical evergreen forests correlate with very high rainfall zones. Hence 1, 2 and 3.

q: India's first Special Economic Zone (SEZ) was established at:
explain: India's first SEZ was established at Kandla (Gandhidham) in Gujarat in 1965, making it one of the world's first SEZs. The SEZ policy was formalized in 2000 and the SEZ Act was passed in 2005.

q: India's latitude extends approximately from:
explain: India's mainland extends from 8°4'N (Kanyakumari) to 37°6'N (Kashmir) in latitude, and 68°7'E to 97°25'E in longitude. With islands, it extends to about 6°45'N (Great Nicobar).

q: Laterite soils are found mainly in:
opts: Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, Nilgiris, Meghalaya (high rainfall)
explain: Laterite soils form in hot, wet tropical regions with alternating wet and dry seasons. Found on the summits and slopes of Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, hills of Odisha, and Meghalaya plateau. Low in nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium — leached heavily.

q: The Periyar National Park (Kerala) is also called:
opts: Thekkady (and it is part of Periyar Tiger Reserve)
explain: Periyar National Park is popularly known as Thekkady. The Periyar Tiger Reserve (1978) includes the national park. It is famous for its boat rides on Periyar Lake where elephants and other wildlife can be spotted.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
explain: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia (1,642 m deep) is the world's deepest lake. It contains about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water. It is also the world's oldest lake (25-30 million years old).

q: The 'Jet Stream' is:
opts: A narrow band of fast-moving air in the upper troposphere
explain: The Jet Stream is a narrow, fast-moving band of air (wind speed 100-300 km/h) in the upper troposphere/lower stratosphere at 7-16 km altitude. It influences weather patterns, aviation routes, and the Indian monsoon.

q: The Mangrove forests in India are most extensive in:
explain: The Sundarbans in West Bengal (and Bangladesh) contain the world's largest mangrove forest (10,000 km²). India has significant mangrove coverage in Odisha, Gujarat (Gulf of Kutch), Tamil Nadu (Pichavaram), and Kerala (Vembanad).

q: The Amazon rainforest is primarily in:
explain: The Amazon rainforest (world's largest tropical rainforest, ~5.5 million sq km) is primarily in Brazil (60%), plus Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Bolivia, and other South American countries.

q: Which is the national river of India?
explain: Ganga was declared the National River of India in 2008. It has deep religious, cultural, and economic significance.

q: The northeast monsoon (October-December) brings rain mainly to:
opts: Tamil Nadu coast and southern Andhra Pradesh
explain: Tamil Nadu receives most of its annual rainfall (about 60%) from the retreating Northeast Monsoon (Oct-Dec), as the Bay of Bengal branch brings moisture to the Coromandel coast. This is why Tamil Nadu has its main rainy season in Oct-Dec.

q: The Great Barrier Reef is in:
explain: The Great Barrier Reef (world's largest coral reef system, 2,300 km long) is off the coast of Queensland, Australia, in the Coral Sea. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: The Amazon river (by volume/discharge) is:
opts: The world's largest river by water volume
explain: The Amazon is the world's largest river by volume/discharge — it accounts for about 20% of all freshwater flowing into the world's oceans. The Nile is longer, but the Amazon carries far more water.

q: The Godavari is called the 'Dakshin Ganga' because:
opts: It is the largest river in Peninsular India
explain: Godavari is called Dakshin Ganga (Ganga of the South) because it is the largest and most sacred river in Peninsular India, originating from Trimbak near Nashik, Maharashtra, flowing 1,465 km to the Bay of Bengal.

q: India's largest tea-producing state is:
explain: Assam is India's largest tea-producing state (about 53% of India's tea). Assam, West Bengal (Darjeeling), and Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris) are the three major tea-growing regions in India.

q: The most fertile soil in India is:
explain: Alluvial soil (deposited by rivers) is the most fertile in India. It covers the Gangetic plains, Brahmaputra valley, and coastal plains. Rich in potash and lime. Supports wheat, rice, sugarcane, oilseeds. Divided into Khadar (new, lighter) and Bangar (old, darker).

q: Which is the largest lake in India?
explain: Chilika Lake (Odisha) is the largest coastal lagoon and the largest lake in India by area (around 1,100 sq km).

q: The Idukki Dam (arch dam) in Kerala is on:
explain: Idukki Dam is a double curvature arch dam on the Periyar river in Kerala's Idukki district. It is India's largest arch dam. The nearby Cheruthoni and Kulamavu dams form the Idukki Hydroelectric Project.

q: Which mountain range is called the 'backbone of India'?
explain: The Vindhya Range (running east-west across central India from Gujarat to Bihar) is often called the 'backbone of India' as it historically divided the Indian subcontinent into North India and South India (Deccan).

q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
explain: The Kosi river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to devastating floods it causes by frequently changing its course.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar separates:
explain: The Strait of Gibraltar (14 km wide at its narrowest) separates Spain (Europe) from Morocco (Africa). It connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea. Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory.

q:
Statement-I: Air transport is the fastest but most expensive mode of transport in India.
Statement-II: Air transport requires the least infrastructure investment per route compared to roadways and railways.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
explain: Statement-I is correct — air transport is indeed the fastest and costliest mode. Statement-II is incorrect/irrelevant as an explanation — air transport's high cost stems from fuel, aircraft and operational costs, not from infrastructure investment being 'least' (airport infrastructure is in fact capital-intensive).

q: The retreat of the southwest monsoon begins from:
explain: The southwest monsoon retreats (withdraws) from India starting from Rajasthan/northwestern India in September, and completely withdraws from India by early December (it retreats southward).

q: Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan Canal) brings water from:
explain: Indira Gandhi Canal (650 km) draws water from the Harike Barrage at the Sutlej-Beas confluence (Punjab) and brings it to arid western Rajasthan, transforming the Thar Desert into cultivable land.

q: The capital of Canada is:
explain: Ottawa (Ontario) is the capital of Canada. Toronto is the largest city and financial capital. Ottawa was chosen as capital by Queen Victoria in 1857 as a compromise between Toronto (Ontario) and Montreal (Quebec).

q: The Jayakwadi (Nathsagar) reservoir in Maharashtra is on:
explain: Jayakwadi (Nathsagar) reservoir is on the Godavari river in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district, Marathwada, Maharashtra. It is one of Maharashtra's largest reservoirs.

q: The Chennai Metro was inaugurated in:
explain: Chennai Metro Rail was inaugurated on 29 June 2015 by PM Narendra Modi. Phase 1 covers about 45 km. Phase 2 is under construction to expand the network to about 118 km.

q: The International Date Line roughly follows:
opts: The 180° meridian (with deviations for island nations)
explain: The International Date Line (IDL) roughly follows the 180° meridian in the Pacific Ocean, but deviates to avoid splitting countries. Going west across the IDL, the date advances by one day. Going east, the date goes back by one day.

q: The Tapi (Tapti) river flows westward through:
opts: Maharashtra, MP, and Gujarat into Arabian Sea
explain: Tapi (Tapti) river (724 km) originates from Satpura Range (MP), flows westward through Vidarbha (Maharashtra), Surat (Gujarat), and drains into the Arabian Sea. Ukai dam is on the Tapi in Gujarat.

q: The 'Walker Circulation' is related to:
opts: East-west circulation over the tropical Pacific
explain: Walker Circulation is the large-scale east-west atmospheric circulation over the tropical Pacific Ocean. Normally, it drives warm water westward and brings upwelling cold water to Peru's coast. During El Niño, it weakens, collapsing the pressure gradient.

q: The Brahmaputra river has which other names?
explain: Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo in Tibet, enters India as Siang/Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, becomes Brahmaputra in Assam, and is called Jamuna in Bangladesh. One of the world's largest rivers by discharge.

q: Lakshadweep islands are formed by:
explain: Lakshadweep islands are coral atolls — formed by coral reefs growing on submerged volcanic peaks. They are located in the Arabian Sea and are India's smallest Union Territory.

q: India's largest thermal power plant is:
explain: Vindhyachal Super Thermal Power Station in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh (4,760 MW installed capacity) is India's largest operational thermal power station.

q: Tamil Nadu's literacy rate (Census 2011) was approximately:
explain: Tamil Nadu had a literacy rate of 80.3% in Census 2011 (Male: 86.8%, Female: 73.9%), higher than the national average of 74.04%. Tamil Nadu consistently performs above the national average in literacy.

q: Which state has the most number of tiger reserves in India?
explain: Madhya Pradesh has the most tiger reserves (7) and the highest tiger population in India. Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Satpura, Panna, Bori-Satpura, and Ratapani are in MP. MP is called the 'Tiger State of India'.

q: The Deccan Plateau is located in which part of India?
explain: The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau in peninsular (southern) India. It covers most of southern and central India.

q: The Mariana Trench (deepest point on Earth, ~11,034 m) is in:
explain: The Mariana Trench is in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Mariana Islands. Challenger Deep (10,929 m in the Mariana Trench) is the deepest known point on Earth.

q: Which type of rainfall is most common in India?
explain: Most of India's rainfall is orographic/relief rainfall caused by moisture-laden monsoon winds rising over mountains (Western Ghats, Himalayas) and cooling. Convectional rain occurs in summer afternoons. Cyclonic rain occurs in coastal areas.

q: The river Brahmaputra is known as 'Tsangpo' in:
explain: The Brahmaputra originates from Chemayungdung glacier in Tibet (China) as the Tsangpo. It enters India in Arunachal Pradesh (called Siang/Dihang), flows through Assam as Brahmaputra, and enters Bangladesh as Jamuna.

q: The Himalayan rivers are 'antecedent' rivers because:
opts: They were formed after the Himalayas
They existed before the Himalayas rose — they cut through the mountains as they uplifted
They are younger than peninsular rivers
explain: Antecedent rivers (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra and their tributaries) are older than the Himalayas. As the Himalayas rose gradually, these rivers maintained their original courses and cut deep gorges through the rising mountains.

q: The Deccan Traps are associated with which geological event?
opts: Massive volcanic eruptions (~66 million years ago)
explain: Deccan Traps formed from massive volcanic eruptions ~66 million years ago, covering ~500,000 sq km in basaltic lava flows. Some scientists link these eruptions (along with Chicxulub asteroid impact) to the mass extinction of dinosaurs.

q: The Middle (Lesser) Himalayas include famous ranges like:
opts: Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat, Mussoorie-Nag Tibba
explain: Middle Himalayas (Himachal) include Pir Panjal (J&K), Dhauladhar (HP), Mahabharat Range (Nepal), and Nag Tibba-Mussoorie Range (Uttarakhand). Average elevation: 3,500-4,500 m. Famous hill stations are here.

q: The Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of India extends up to:
explain: India's EEZ extends 200 nautical miles (370 km) from its coastline into the sea. Within the EEZ, India has exclusive rights to explore and exploit marine resources (fish, minerals, energy).

q: India is situated on which tectonic plate?
explain: India sits on the Indo-Australian Plate. The collision of this plate with the Eurasian Plate formed the Himalayas.

q: Tamil Nadu's main crop and what it depends on:
opts: Rice, depends primarily on northeast monsoon (Oct-Dec) and Kaveri/other rivers
explain: Rice is Tamil Nadu's main crop. Tamil Nadu's agriculture depends heavily on the northeast monsoon (Oct-Dec) unlike most of India (which depends on southwest monsoon). The Kaveri delta (Thanjavur) is the 'Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu'.

q:
With reference to volcanoes, consider the following statements:
1. The 'Ring of Fire' around the Pacific Ocean contains most of the world's active volcanoes.
2. Shield volcanoes are typically formed by highly viscous, silica-rich lava that erupts explosively.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — shield volcanoes (e.g., Hawaiian volcanoes) form from low-viscosity, basaltic lava that flows gently, not explosive silica-rich lava (that describes composite/stratovolcanoes).

q: Which river is called 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
explain: The Kosi river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of the devastating floods it causes annually. It frequently changes course and causes enormous loss of life and property.

q: The 'Project Elephant' was launched to protect elephants in:
explain: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 by the Government of India to protect elephants, their habitats, and migration corridors. India has 27,000+ wild elephants (60% of Asian elephants). The Asian Elephant is India's National Heritage Animal.

q: 'Isobars' on a weather map connect places having:
explain: Isobars connect places having the same atmospheric pressure on a weather map. They help identify high-pressure (anticyclones) and low-pressure (cyclones) areas. Closely-spaced isobars indicate strong winds.

q: Which of the following lakes is famous for rose-colored water?
explain: Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan) — India's largest inland saltwater lake — sometimes appears pinkish due to salt-loving microorganisms (halophytes). It is the main source of salt in Rajasthan and a Ramsar wetland site.

q: The Vindhya-Satpura uplift (central Indian range system) is important because:
opts: It divides India into North and Peninsular India (historical boundary)
It is the highest range in central India
It is a young fold mountain range
explain: The Vindhya-Satpura ranges historically separated North India from the Deccan. They form the northern boundary of the Peninsular Plateau. The Narmada-Son rift valley separates the two.

q: The Silent Valley National Park (Kerala) is famous for:
opts: Untouched evergreen forest and lion-tailed macaques
explain: Silent Valley National Park in Palakkad district, Kerala, in the Nilgiri Hills is famous for being the last undisturbed tropical moist evergreen forest in South India, home to the endangered lion-tailed macaque.

q: 'Loo' is a type of wind in India that refers to:
opts: Hot, dry summer winds over north India
explain: Loo winds are hot (45–48°C), dry, dusty local winds that blow in the afternoons during summer (May-June) across the north Indian plains (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan). They cause heatstroke and can be fatal.

q: Singareni Coalfields are in:
explain: Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) operates coal mines in Telangana (formerly Andhra Pradesh). Singareni is the only government-owned coal company owned jointly by the State (51%) and Centre (49%).

q: The Shivalik Hills form the:
opts: Outermost and youngest foothills of the Himalayas
explain: Shivalik Hills (Outer Himalayas, average 900-1,200 m) are the youngest and outermost foothills of the Himalayan system. They run along the entire Himalayan range from Punjab to Arunachal Pradesh.

q: Duncan Passage separates:
explain: Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman. The Ten Degree Channel separates Andaman Islands from Nicobar Islands. The Nine Degree Channel separates Lakshadweep Islands.

q: India's total forest cover is approximately (as per FSI 2021):
opts: About 24% of India's total geographical area
explain: India's forest and tree cover is about 24.62% of total geographical area as per Forest Survey of India (FSI) State of Forest Report 2021. The National Forest Policy (1988) mandates 33% forest cover — this target has not been achieved.

q: The Western Coastal Plains include:
explain: Western Coastal Plains stretch from Gujarat in the north to Kanyakumari. Includes: Kathiawar-Kutch coast (Gujarat), Konkan Coast (Maharashtra/Goa), Karnataka coast, and Malabar Coast (Kerala).

q: El Niño affects Indian monsoon by:
explain: El Niño (warming of central/eastern Pacific Ocean) weakens the Walker Circulation, suppresses Indian monsoon convection, and typically leads to below-normal monsoon rainfall in India — causing droughts. La Niña has the opposite effect (stronger monsoon).

q: Which is India's longest road tunnel?
opts: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (Banihal-Qazigund, J&K)
explain: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (Banihal-Qazigund Tunnel, 8.45 km rail tunnel) is part of the J&K railway. The Atal (Rohtang) Road Tunnel (9.02 km) is currently India's longest road tunnel.

q: The soils of the Deccan Plateau are mainly:
explain: Black cotton soils (regur soils) are formed from Deccan trap (basaltic lava). They are highly fertile, clay-rich, moisture-retentive, and ideal for cotton cultivation. Found in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat.
